--- ## 💡 The idea Most trading bots either chase every signal or need a quant team to configure. This one follows a simple, explainable discipline that long-term investors already use: buy quality stocks when they pull back to their moving averages, add when fear is high and the earnings still hold up, trim when prices run too far, never panic-sell into uncertainty, and always keep a cash reserve. Four agents check the market, the calendar, the company and the news; a deterministic risk manager has the final word on every order. **How it did.** On 2026 so far, reading the news that ships with the package, the agent made **+15.9%** against SPY's +12.1%, with a Sharpe ratio of 1.70 against 0.77, and its worst drop was **-5.3%** against SPY's -8.9% ([details](#2026-so-far-with-news)). From 2018 to 2026 it earned less than SPY in the long bull market, 10.4% a year against 14.1%, and fell about half as far, -18.2% against -33.7% ([details](#-backtest)). > Not financial advice. It starts in paper mode, and live trading needs three explicit switches. ## Four ways to use it | | **Dashboard** | **Command line** | **AI assistants (MCP)** | **Python** | |---|---|---|---|---| | Start with | `riskaware dashboard` | `riskaware scan` | `riskaware mcp-setup claude-desktop --apply` | `from riskaware.research import run_experiment` | | What you do | watch the regime, the signals, the agents and the backtests, in English or 中文 | scan, backtest, paper trade, and schedule the agents | describe a strategy in words; Claude, Codex or Gemini write it, test it and explain the result | run experiments on the frozen 2020, 2022 and 2026 markets and keep a record for a paper | | Needs | the `dashboard` extra | nothing else | the `mcp` extra; runs on your plan, no API key | nothing else | ```python from riskaware.research import Experiment, run_experiment r = run_experiment(Experiment(strategy="swing_trend", news=True, split="2026-07-01")) print(r.summary()["metrics"], r.leak, r.folder) ``` --- ## ✨ Feature tour The highlights. The guides in [docs/](docs/) cover every command and setting, and the [website](https://jackson-cmd.github.io/risk-aware-trading-agents/) has longer answers on news backtesting, point-in-time data and LLM agents. ### 🧠 How it works - **Macro-aware market regimes.** VIX and its term structure (VIX/VIX3M), sector breadth, credit appetite (HYG vs IEF), safe-haven demand, a fear-and-greed gauge computed from free data (and CNN's Fear & Greed for reference), and the **FOMC, CPI, jobs report, PPI, GDP and PCE** calendar put the market in one of four regimes: risk-on, neutral, uncertain, risk-off. - **Buy low, sell high.** Pullbacks to **EMA 50 / 100 / 200**, RSI(2) and z-score mean reversion, **quality dips that must pass an earnings check** (revenue growth, margins, free cash flow, leverage, EPS beats), breakouts and trend continuation in strong markets. Take-profit trims when a stock runs far above EMA50; trend exits after a break of a falling EMA50. - **No panic selling.** When the regime is uncertain or risk-off the agent holds, does not sell, and only buys at strong support. Only a disaster the company itself confirms (bankruptcy, delisting, restatement in its own 8-K or press release) or an optional hard stop can force an exit. - **Risk first.** A **30% cash + T-bill floor**, position, sector and speculative ("lottery ticket") caps, volatility-scaled sizes, buying in tranches, a Treasury sleeve for conservative profiles, idle cash parked in a T-bill ETF, a drawdown pause, a kill switch. - **Optional LLM review, per agent.** A bull analyst, a bear analyst and a risk judge (GPT, Claude, any OpenAI-compatible model such as DeepSeek or Qwen, or a free local model through Ollama) can nudge conviction by at most ±0.15 or veto a buy. They can never create a trade or change a limit. News reaches them only as quoted, untrusted text, and every prompt and reply is kept in the local journal so you can see how each decision was made. ```mermaid flowchart TB D["Prices · VIX · sectors · FOMC / CPI / NFP calendar · earnings · Finviz + RSS + SEC"] M["Macro agent
regime + fear/greed"] E["Event agent
FOMC, CPI, jobs"] T["Technical agent
EMA 50/100/200,
mean reversion, trend"] F["Fundamental agent
earnings quality"] N["News agent
cross-verified"] S["Strategy: built-in or yours"] L["Optional LLM
bull / bear / judge"] R["Risk manager: cash floor · caps · tranches · regime rules"] D --> M & E & T & F & N M & E & T & F & N --> S L -.->|"±0.15 at most"| S S --> R R --> G["Safety guards"] --> B["Paper or live broker"] R --> X["Backtester"] ``` #### What the agent does in each regime | Regime | Typical trigger | Buys | Sells | Size | |---|---|---|---|---| | 🟢 **Risk-on** | SPY above a rising EMA50 and EMA200, VIX < 20, most sectors above EMA200 | pullbacks, breakouts, dips | take profit, trend exits | 100% | | ⚪ **Neutral** | none of the others | EMA support, mean reversion, quality dips | take profit | 75% | | 🟡 **Uncertain** | 2 days before an FOMC decision, the day before CPI or the jobs report, VIX 20–30, fear gauge < 35, downtrend | EMA100 / EMA200 support only | **none: hold** | 50% | | 🔴 **Risk-off** | VIX ≥ 30, VIX backwardation below EMA200, credit stress | quality dips and broad ETFs, small tranches | **none: hold** | 35% | Emergency exits (a severe red flag the company itself confirms in its 8-K or its own press release, or the profile's hard stop) work in every regime. #### Risk profiles | | Conservative | Balanced | Aggressive | |---|---|---|---| | Cash + T-bill floor | 30% | 30% | 30% | | Treasury sleeve (IEF) | 15% | 5% | 0% | | Max single stock / sector | 5% / 20% | 7% / 25% | 10% / 35% | | Speculative sleeve (high-volatility names) | 0% | 3% (2 names) | 7% (3 names) | | Minimum conviction | 0.65 | 0.58 | 0.52 | | Earnings score needed for a dip buy | 70 | 60 | 50 | | Take-profit trigger | +20% | +25% | +30% | | Breakout entries | off | off | on | Every limit can be overridden in `riskaware.yaml`. Positions are built in tranches (50% / 25% / 25% of the target); a later tranche needs a deeper support touch or a winning position, and trimmed positions can be rebuilt on the next pullback. ### 📰 Cross-verified news - **Sources.** Finviz (free), Google News, Nasdaq, Seeking Alpha and Yahoo RSS, plus the company's own **SEC 8-K filings**. - **Confirmed means two sources.** A story only counts toward the company it names, and it is confirmed when two independent outlets, the company's own press release or its SEC filing carry it. A red flag on a confirmed story blocks new buys. - **Hard to fool.** Only the company's 8-K, or its own release confirming what independent outlets reported first, can force a sale, so a fake headline, a fake press release and the outlets that repeat it, or another company's bad news cannot. A denial clears the story it refutes instead of confirming it. The same check runs in backtests, on news replayed as it was published: see [News in backtests](#news-in-backtests). ### 🤖 Paper-trading agents An agent is a strategy with its own paper account. Pick a strategy (built-in or your own file), a risk profile, a stock list and the starting cash, and the agent trades that account once every trading day on free Yahoo Finance prices. Run several side by side and see which one beats SPY. Agents only ever use the built-in paper account, never a broker. ```bash riskaware agents init # steady, momentum, breakout, fear-buyer riskaware agents add dips --strategy rsi2 --universe tech --cash 25000 riskaware agents add mine --strategy my_dip.py:MyDip --profile aggressive riskaware agents add luna --strategy risk_aware --llm openai:gpt-5.6-luna # with an LLM review board riskaware agents add local --strategy risk_aware --llm ollama:qwen2.5:3b # a free local model riskaware agents run # trade every active agent now riskaware agents why luna # how it decided: setups, risk check, bull / bear / judge riskaware agents # the leaderboard riskaware agents schedule --install # every trading day, by itself ``` The daily job (a LaunchAgent on macOS, a crontab line on Linux, a scheduled task on Windows) wakes every 15 minutes on weekdays and trades each agent once per trading day after 15:40 New York time, before the close. It skips holidays, catches up after the laptop sleeps, and keeps going when one agent fails. Each agent keeps its account, journal and daily equity in `~/.riskaware/arena/NAME/`. The **Agents** page of the dashboard shows the leaderboard and lets you create, run, pause, reset and delete agents; its **Decisions** tab shows how each decision was made, including the LLM's bull case, bear case and verdict and the exact prompt it was sent. GPT needs `OPENAI_API_KEY` in your `.env`; a local model needs [Ollama](https://ollama.com) (`ollama pull qwen2.5:3b`); and `--llm claude-cli`, `codex-cli` or `gemini-cli` uses your Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini plan through its command-line tool, with no API key. More in [docs/agents.md](docs/agents.md). ### 🔗 MCP server `riskaware mcp` serves the agents over the Model Context Protocol, so Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor or any MCP client can use them, on your plan and without an API key. `riskaware mcp-setup` prints (or, with `--apply`, runs) the one step that connects it: ```bash pip install risk-aware-trading-agents # the MCP server is part of the base install since 0.7.2 riskaware mcp-setup claude-desktop --apply # or: claude-code, codex (your ChatGPT login), gemini, antigravity ``` Other ways in: in Claude Desktop, download `risk-aware-trading-agents-.mcpb` from the [latest release](https://github.com/jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents/releases/latest) and open it. A client that starts servers by command can use `uvx risk-aware-trading-agents mcp` (nothing to install first) or `docker run -i --rm ghcr.io/jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents mcp`. The server is listed on the official MCP Registry as `io.github.jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents`. Twenty-one tools: `market_regime`, `scan`, `analyze_stock`, `stock_news`, `list_strategies`, `backtest`, `strategy_guide`, `backtest_code`, `agents_leaderboard`, `agent_detail`, `agent_decisions`, `agents_create` and `agents_run`, and for research `research_guide`, `market_day`, `run_experiment`, `list_experiments`, `experiment_report`, `trading_session_start`, `trading_session_step` and `trading_session_status`. They are read-only or act on local paper accounts; no tool can send an order to a broker. Then just ask, for example "What regime is the market in, and what is coming up this week?" or "Backtest the wheel on megacap with $1M since 2018." ChatGPT itself only connects to remote servers, so on the OpenAI side use Codex, which runs on your ChatGPT login. More in [docs/agents.md](docs/agents.md#use-it-from-claude-chatgpt-or-gemini-mcp). ### 🧪 Strategy lab Describe a strategy in plain words and let the AI build it. Over MCP, Claude, Codex or Gemini read `strategy_guide`, write the strategy as a Python class and run it with `backtest_code`. Before the code runs, the lab refuses dates and stock tickers written into it (both let a backtest know the future), files, network and private attributes. Then it backtests the code in a separate process with no API keys and a time limit, and returns the metrics next to SPY and buy-and-hold, or the lines to fix. > Write a strategy that buys two-day pullbacks in uptrends when the recent news is positive, and sells after 10 days or at +8%. Backtest it on the tech list for 2026 with news. `save_as` keeps a strategy that works: it then shows up on the dashboard and can run as a paper agent. For code from anywhere else, `riskaware lab my_strategy.py --preset tech` does the same checks and backtest. More in [docs/strategy-lab.md](docs/strategy-lab.md). ### 🏆 LLM trading agent leaderboard [**rta-bench-1**](https://jackson-cmd.github.io/risk-aware-trading-agents/leaderboard.html) ranks LLMs as trading agents on the same game: the 56 large caps, after every fifth close, through 2026 to date, the 2022 bear market and the 2020 crash, each played blind and with real names, on news replayed by the minute it was published and with realistic fill costs. A model's training cutoff decides which scores count: periods after the cutoff are ranked, periods it may remember are listed apart. For each model the board shows how it made its money (market and style exposure against stock picking, sectors, holding periods, trades set off by news) and a memory score, next to the five rule strategies, SPY and the equal-weight list. An entry is one JSON file with the model's replies, so anyone can replay it without calling the model; to add a model, run `riskaware research submit` and open a pull request. More in [docs/leaderboard.md](docs/leaderboard.md). ### 🔬 Research kit Three very different years ship with the package, frozen, for experiments that anyone can repeat: **2026** to date (a rising market), **2022** (the rate-hike bear market: SPY -18.2%) and **2020** (the COVID crash: SPY -34% in 23 days, then a new high). Each has daily prices for the 64 stocks and 25 ETFs from two years before it, the VIX term structure, that year's headlines, and every indicator and regime reading the agents use, each as it was known at that day's close. | Period | Test window | News for the 64 stocks | |---|---|---| | `2026` (default) | 2026-01-02 to 2026-11-11 | 16,945 Benzinga headlines and SEC 8-K filings | | `2022` | the whole year | 29,300 Benzinga headlines | | `2020` | the whole year | 19,618 Benzinga headlines | They are cut from a local archive of about 3.2 million Benzinga headlines from 2011 to 2026 (about 202,000 in 2020, 270,000 in 2022 and 250,000 in 2026), enough to backtest agents that read the news and to look for news factors. The 2026 files are also on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/jacksonwangpro1/point-in-time-market-data-2026), as Parquet with a data viewer and the original files. ```bash riskaware research day 2026-04-08 --symbols NVDA,TSLA # everything known at that close riskaware research run --strategy swing_trend --split 2026-07-01 riskaware research run --strategy swing_trend --period 2022 # the bear market riskaware research trade --llm ollama:qwen2.5:3b --universe core --blind --period 2020 ``` - **Point in time.** Signals at the close, orders at the next open: swing trading on daily bars. A headline counts only after it was published, and indicators only look back. - **A look-ahead check on every run.** The run is repeated with every price and headline after three cut days replaced by random ones, and the decisions before each cut must not change. For an LLM it replays the model's replies and checks that what the model was shown before each cut did not change, so the model is not asked twice. - **A record for papers.** Each run saves its data hashes, code, settings, metrics, bootstrap intervals, trades and every decision. - **Made for LLMs.** Over MCP, describe a strategy and Claude writes and tests it (`run_experiment`), looks at any day (`market_day`), or trades a period step by step (`trading_session_start`), blind if you like: no tickers, company names or dates. Five common swing strategies on the 56 megacaps, at most 10 equal positions; return without news / with news: | Strategy | 2026 (to Nov 11) | 2022 | 2020 | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Trend following (EMA20 / EMA50 cross) | **+21.1%** / +19.6% | -6.0% / -5.0% | +36.6% / **+68.4%** | | Post-news drift (without news: the same trade on a price jump) | +15.7% / +4.4% | -13.3% / -14.1% | +9.4% / +28.4% | | Connors RSI(2) | +12.7% / +10.8% | -2.2% / -5.7% | +14.0% / +12.7% | | Pullback in an uptrend | +2.3% / +1.7% | **-4.7% / -4.0%** | +2.3% / +3.3% | | 20-day breakout | -0.3% / -3.5% | -12.8% / -13.7% | +33.1% / +30.4% | | SPY buy and hold | +12.1% | -18.6% | +17.2% | | Equal weight, the same 56 stocks | +11.4% | -12.4% | +40.1% | No rule wins every year. Trend following led in the two rising years; in 2022 every strategy lost money, all of them less than SPY, and the pullback rule lost least. The news filter cut returns in 2026 and seemed to help in 2020, but the 2020 gain is one position: with news, a free slot let trend following buy Tesla in April 2020 and hold it to the end of the year. The equal-weight row shows the survivorship bias of today's large caps, largest in 2020. Every interval overlaps, and every run passed the look-ahead check. Definitions, the full tables with 95% intervals, and advice for papers in [docs/research.md](docs/research.md). ### 📊 Backtest Built-in strategy, balanced profile, the 55-stock `megacap` list, $100k, signals at the close and fills the next day, 5 bps slippage, January 2018 to November 2026: | | risk_aware | SPY buy & hold | |---|---|---| | CAGR | 10.4% | 14.1% | | Volatility | 9.3% | 19.0% | | Sharpe | 0.84 | 0.66 | | Max drawdown | -18.2% | -33.7% | | Worst calendar year | -3.7% | -18.2% | | Average stocks / cash + T-bills | 57% / 39% | 100% / 0% | Read it honestly: in a long bull market the agent earns less than the index because it keeps at least 30% in cash, and it loses roughly half as much when markets fall. The list is today's large caps, so it carries survivorship bias; these numbers use neither news nor fundamentals (2026 with news is below), and past results do not predict future ones. Reproduce it with `riskaware backtest --compare buy_and_hold`. ```bash riskaware backtest --strategy risk_aware --compare buy_and_hold,ema_bounce,rsi2 --start 2018-01-01 --open riskaware backtest --preset etf --profile conservative riskaware backtest --symbols AAPL,MSFT,NVDA,COST --cash 25000 riskaware backtest --synthetic # offline demo, no download ``` Every run writes a self-contained HTML report (metrics, equity and drawdown charts with regime shading, monthly returns, every trade with its reason) plus CSV files. #### 2026 so far, with news The same agent and settings on 2026, from January 2 to November 11, now reading the news that ships with the package: 15,542 Benzinga headlines and 605 SEC filings for these 56 stocks, each day only what was out before its close. | January 2 – November 11, 2026 | risk_aware + news | risk_aware, no news | SPY buy & hold | |---|---|---|---| | Return | **+15.9%** | +15.4% | +12.1% | | Volatility | 8.2% | 7.8% | 14.0% | | Sharpe | 1.70 | 1.73 | 0.77 | | Max drawdown | **-5.3%** | -5.3% | -8.9% | | Average stocks / cash + T-bills | 60% / 35% | 61% / 34% | 100% / 0% | The agent beat SPY by 3.8 points while holding stocks with 60% of its money on average, and its worst drop was 60% of SPY's: in the March sell-off it fell 5.3% while SPY fell 8.9%. News added half a point of return this year. Ten months is a short test, so the 2018–2026 table above is still the better guide. Reproduce it with `riskaware backtest --preset megacap --start 2026-01-02 --end 2026-11-11 --news`. #### News in backtests A backtest may only use news it would have seen on that day, so it needs each item's publication time. News for 2020, 2022 and 2026 ships with the package for the 64 stocks of the built-in lists: 19,618, 29,300 and 16,945 items (Benzinga headlines, titles only; for 2026 also SEC 8-K filings, January 1 to November 11). For other years, `riskaware news-history` keeps an archive on your own machine (`~/.riskaware/news`, never in the repository). `--news` replays both through the same clustering and two-source check used in live trading. Each day sees only items published before its close (16:00 New York, 13:00 on early-close days), and orders fill the next day. ```bash riskaware backtest --strategy examples/strategies/news_earnings_drift.py --preset megacap --start 2026-01-02 --news # 2026: nothing to download riskaware news-history build --preset core --contact-email you@example.com # SEC 8-K filings since 2018 riskaware news-history build --symbols AAPL,NVDA --source benzinga # with your own BENZINGA_API_KEY riskaware news-history import my_news.csv --tz America/New_York # timestamp, symbol, headline[, source, url, sentiment] riskaware news-history status riskaware news-history show NVDA --date 2024-05-22 # what the backtest saw at that close riskaware backtest --strategy examples/strategies/news_earnings_drift.py --preset core --news --compare buy_and_hold ``` | Source | What goes into the archive | Cost | |---|---|---| | Bundled with the package | 2020, 2022 and 2026 Benzinga headlines (titles only), and 2026 SEC 8-K filings, for the 64 stocks of the built-in lists | free, already installed | | SEC EDGAR | every 8-K (earnings, officer changes, deals, impairments, restatements) with SEC's acceptance time | free; SEC asks for a contact email | | Benzinga | headlines from your own news API key | your Benzinga plan | | CSV | any news you have the right to use | — | The `core` preset is SPY, QQQ, AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, AMZN, GOOGL, META and TSLA. SPY and QQQ are funds, not companies, so the SEC archive has little or nothing for them; the FOMC, CPI and jobs calendar already drives the regime in every backtest. Benzinga counts as one publisher, so a Benzinga-only story stays single-source until an SEC filing or a second publisher backs it. What you download or import stays on your machine. Details: [docs/news-history.md](docs/news-history.md). **More history.** We keep a much larger archive, about 3.2 million Benzinga headlines from 2011 to 2026 (about 200,000 to 300,000 a year). It is far too big to ship in the package, so the package carries 2020, 2022 and 2026 for the built-in lists. If you need more years or more stocks, open an issue and we will look at how to provide them, for example as a separate download. ### 📚 Strategy library Every built-in strategy runs through the same risk manager, so all of them keep the cash floor. Backtest any of them with `riskaware backtest --strategy NAME`; compare several with `--compare a,b,c`. | Strategy | Type | Idea | |---|---|---| | `risk_aware` | stocks (default) | the multi-agent strategy described above | | `momentum_rotation` | stocks | each month hold the strongest names by 6-month relative strength, above EMA200 | | `donchian_breakout` | stocks | Turtle-style: 55-day highs on volume, exit on a 20-day low | | `bollinger_reversion` | stocks | buy closes below the lower Bollinger band in uptrends, sell at the middle band | | `fear_greed_dca` | stocks / ETFs | buy in steps when fear is high, trim in extreme greed | | `ema_bounce`, `rsi2`, `golden_cross`, `buy_and_hold` | stocks | simple references and baselines | | `swing_trend`, `swing_rsi2`, `swing_breakout`, `swing_pullback`, `swing_news` | stocks | five textbook swing strategies with a news switch, the [research kit](#-research-kit)'s baselines | | `aggressive_calls` | options | buy ~0.6-delta calls 45–60 days out on pullbacks in strong uptrends; +100% take profit, -50% stop | | `wheel` | options | sell ~0.25-delta cash-secured puts near support; after assignment, sell covered calls above cost | Backtests from January 2018 to November 2026 on the `megacap` list: | Strategy | Profile, capital | CAGR | Sharpe | Max drawdown | Worst year | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `wheel` | aggressive, $1M | 14.1% | 1.12 | -21.7% | +5.8% | | `momentum_rotation` | balanced, $100k | 12.5% | 0.91 | -18.2% | -8.2% | | `risk_aware` | balanced, $100k | 10.4% | 0.84 | -18.2% | -3.8% | | `donchian_breakout` | balanced, $100k | 9.8% | 0.86 | -12.6% | -6.7% | | `aggressive_calls` | aggressive, $100k | 6.7% | 0.30 | -40.3% | -24.7% | | `bollinger_reversion` | balanced, $100k | 4.5% | 0.58 | -4.4% | +0.8% | | SPY buy & hold | | 14.1% | 0.66 | -33.7% | -18.2% | #### Options (backtest only) Option strategies open long calls or puts, cash-secured puts and covered calls. The risk manager caps the premium in long options (`options_sleeve`: 0% conservative, 3% balanced, 12% aggressive; `options_per_trade`: 0 / 1% / 3%), keeps put collateral out of the 30% cash floor and inside the single-stock cap, and never lets shares that back a written call be sold. Expiring options settle at intrinsic value; written puts are assigned into shares, covered calls are called away. There is no free archive of historical option quotes, so the backtester prices options with Black-Scholes on a modelled implied volatility (VIX for index ETFs; realized volatility, a 10% volatility premium and a VIX scaling for stocks) and pays half of a 4% bid-ask spread plus $0.65 per contract. The results move with these assumptions: without the 10% volatility premium the wheel drops to a 0.81 Sharpe and `aggressive_calls` ranges from 3% to 15% a year depending on spread and volatility, always with a drawdown near -40%. Treat option backtests as the shape of a strategy, not a forecast. `riskaware run` skips option orders in this version. Written puts need cash for 100 shares per contract inside the single-stock cap, so the wheel only trades names whose strike × 100 fits (about $10k per name on a $100k aggressive account); test it with `--cash 1000000` or a list of lower-priced names. ### 🧩 Write your own strategy Write one Python method, and the same strategy object runs in backtests, paper trading and live trading with the same risk engine. ```bash riskaware new-strategy my_dip # creates my_dip.py from a template riskaware backtest --strategy my_dip.py --compare risk_aware,buy_and_hold riskaware run --strategy my_dip.py # paper trade it ``` ```python from riskaware.strategy import Action, Signal, Strategy class MyDip(Strategy): name = "my_dip" default_params = {"rsi_entry": 30, "take_profit": 0.20} def on_bar(self, ctx): signals = [] for sym in ctx.universe: row = ctx.row(sym) # indicators at today's close if row is None: continue pos = ctx.position(sym) if pos is None and row["close"] > row["ema200"] and row["rsi14"] < self.params["rsi_entry"]: signals.append(Signal(sym, Action.BUY, strength=0.7, reason="oversold in an uptrend")) elif pos and pos.gain >= self.params["take_profit"]: signals.append(Signal(sym, Action.SELL, strength=0.8, fraction=0.5, reason="take profit")) return signals ``` A strategy only says what it wants and how sure it is; the risk manager decides the size and enforces the cash floor, caps and regime rules, so your strategy inherits the same protection. `ctx.market` has the regime, VIX and upcoming events; `ctx.quality(sym)` and `ctx.news(sym)` give the earnings verdict and the verified news in live runs; `ctx.news` also works in backtests run with `--news`. See [docs/custom-strategies.md](docs/custom-strategies.md). [backtesting with news without look-ahead bias](https://jackson-cmd.github.io/risk-aware-trading-agents/news-backtesting.html) · [point-in-time market data for 2026](https://jackson-cmd.github.io/risk-aware-trading-agents/point-in-time-market-data.html) · [testing LLM trading agents](https://jackson-cmd.github.io/risk-aware-trading-agents/llm-trading-agents.html). ### How do I backtest a trading strategy with news, without look-ahead bias? Run `riskaware backtest --news`, or `riskaware research run` for a record you can cite. News is replayed point in time: each day the strategy sees only the headlines and SEC filings published before that day's 16:00 New York close, and its orders fill at the next open. Every research experiment is also run again with a random future after three cut days, and the decisions before each cut must not change. See [news in backtests](docs/news-history.md) and the [research kit](docs/research.md). ### Where can I get historical news data for backtesting? 2020, 2022 and 2026 ship with the package for 64 large-cap US stocks: 19,618, 29,300 and 16,945 items, Benzinga headlines (titles only; for 2026 also SEC 8-K filings), each with its publication time. For other years, `riskaware news-history build` downloads SEC 8-K filings for free, and Benzinga headlines with your own API key; a CSV with a time, a ticker and a headline works too. See [docs/news-history.md](docs/news-history.md). ### Is there a free point-in-time dataset of US stock prices, VIX and news? Yes. The research kit holds three frozen periods, 2026 to date, 2022 and 2020, each with daily bars for 64 stocks and 25 ETFs from two years before it, the VIX term structure (VIX9D, VIX, VIX3M, VVIX) and that year's news, with SHA-256 hashes so that a paper can cite the exact data. `riskaware research day 2022-06-13` shows everything that was known at that close. See [what ships](docs/research.md#what-ships). ### How do I evaluate an LLM trading agent fairly? Let it trade a frozen period (2026, 2022 or 2020) one decision at a time with `riskaware research trade --llm ...`, or with `trading_session_start` over MCP. Each observation holds only what was known at that close, orders fill at the next open, and the run is saved with every order and its metrics against SPY. Blind mode replaces tickers, company names and dates, so the model cannot recall how a stock did. See [LLM agents](docs/research.md#let-an-llm-trade-a-period). ### Can Claude, ChatGPT (Codex) or Gemini backtest my strategy? Yes, over MCP. Run `riskaware mcp-setup claude-desktop --apply` (or `claude-code`, `codex`, `gemini`), then describe the strategy in words. The assistant writes it as code; the code is checked for dates, tickers and side effects, runs in a separate process, and comes back with metrics, confidence intervals and a look-ahead verdict. See the [MCP server](#-mcp-server) and the [strategy lab](docs/strategy-lab.md). ### Does news sentiment improve swing trading strategies? Not in our 2026 test with headline sentiment from one feed. A news filter made each of five common swing strategies (trend following, RSI(2) mean reversion, breakouts, pullbacks, post-news drift) slightly worse, and buying on positive headlines did worse than buying the same price move without them. Trend following made +21.1% against SPY's +12.1%. See the [results](#-research-kit). ### How do I paper trade before risking real money? Paper trading is the default. `riskaware run` trades the built-in paper account, `riskaware agents` runs several strategies on simulated money every trading day, and broker paper accounts such as Alpaca's work too. Live trading needs three explicit switches. See [safety](#-safety). ### Which brokers are supported? A built-in paper account, Alpaca, Interactive Brokers, Public.com, Charles Schwab, tastytrade, Tradier, Futu/moomoo, Tiger Brokers and Longbridge. See [brokers](#-brokers). ## 🧭 Roadmap - Point-in-time fundamentals from SEC XBRL for backtests - Live option orders (option chains from each broker), protective puts and collars - More brokers (Webull, E*TRADE) and crypto / HK / A-share markets - Walk-forward parameter studies ## 🤝 Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome: new brokers, data sources, strategies, translations. repository.description: Give your AI your whole life. Keep your private things private. Olympus runs on your Mac, Omarchy or Ubuntu 24.04 LTS computer and works with ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Codex, Claude Code and any app that speaks MCP.
repository.name: Olympus
repository.readme:
![Olympus: a towering mountain crowned by a celestial palace, surrounded by cyborg gods, AI agents, and lobster adventurers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/main/assets/olympus-banner.png) # ⛰️ Olympus **Your machine, your memory. Keep your private things private.** Olympus keeps your email, files and messages on your own computer and decides, item by item, what each AI may see. ChatGPT, Claude, Grok and any app that speaks MCP can use it, while your private things stay private. On a Mac, and on [Omarchy](https://omarchy.org) and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS Linux. Free and open source. [![version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.4.2-534AB7)](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-0F6E56)](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/LICENSE) [![tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-3400%2B%20passing-1D9E75)](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) [![openclaw](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenClaw-2026.7.1%2B-378ADD)](https://openclaw.ai) [![runtime](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime-Bun%20%2B%20TypeScript-B45309)](https://bun.sh) [olympusplugin.ai](https://olympusplugin.ai) · [Get started](#get-started) · [Olympus in ChatGPT](#olympus-for-chatgpt) · [Claude, Grok and other apps](#claude-grok-and-other-apps) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Sources](#supported-sources) · [Security model](#the-security-model) · [OpenClaw quickstart](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/docs/QUICKSTART.md) · [Commands](#command-reference) --- > **🤖 Installing this as an AI agent for OpenClaw?** Stop and read > **[INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md](INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md)** before running any > command — it is the step-by-step runbook you must follow, including > exactly what to tell your operator after each step (your install report > must end with the Step 1→2 invitation, never a bare status line). Managed > `git:`, `clawhub:`, and `npm-pack:` installs intentionally hide their internal > package path; use the installed `olympus` CLI and this packaged runbook rather > than searching OpenClaw's managed storage. **Setting up Olympus for ChatGPT, > Claude or Grok instead?** Follow [Get started](#get-started), not this > runbook. --- Frontier AI models are the smartest, but using them means sending your life to someone else's cloud. Local models keep it home, but they are a step behind, and the best ones need an expensive computer under your desk. Olympus gives you both, on the laptop you already have. Every email, file and message is judged, one by one, as **Personal**, **Private** or **Secret**: on your own computer by default, or by Venice's private models if you choose a Venice-only setup. - **Personal:** ChatGPT, Claude or Grok can read the parts that answer your question, and cite them. - **Private:** only a model on your computer reads it (or Venice, if you turn it on); your AI app never gets the item itself. In ChatGPT, only you see the answer; other apps get an answer written from it, which can repeat what it says. - **Secret:** passwords, recovery codes and keys. Once Olympus recognizes a Secret, it is never sent or answered from. Labels are automatic and can be wrong. Everything is stored and searched on your computer: the search index is built there, by a model small enough for a computer with 8 GB of memory. There is no hosted copy of your things, no account and no subscription. Olympus's publisher runs only a relay that passes your AI app's requests to your computer without storing them. Google sign-in happens on your computer, directly with Google. For hard private questions you can reach stronger models: [Venice](https://venice.ai) runs private models that, under Venice's own terms, keep nothing you send, and zkAPI, from OpenAnonymity and the Ethereum Foundation, hides who is asking (see [Stronger models, privately](#stronger-models-privately)). ```text you › "What did I commit to this week, across email and Telegram?" agent › Three commitments: the tax documents to Maria by Friday (email, Tue), reviewing the lease amendment (email, Mon), and the Saturday ride logistics (Telegram, Wed). [3 citations] ``` Your agent saw a bounded, cited, policy-gated answer. It never saw your mailbox. ## Get started You need a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) on macOS 13 Ventura or later, or an x86_64 computer running [Omarchy](https://omarchy.org) or Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. Intel Macs, other Linux distributions and ARM Linux are not supported yet. You do not need OpenClaw, Tailscale, an API key or a new account. **1. Install Olympus on your computer.** On a Mac, open **Terminal** and run: ```bash curl -fsSL https://olympusplugin.ai/install.sh | sh ``` On Omarchy, first install the tools Olympus uses to read scans, photos and voice notes, then run the Linux installer: ```bash sudo pacman -S --needed tesseract tesseract-data-eng poppler libvips libheif ffmpeg curl -fsSL https://olympusplugin.ai/install-linux.sh | sh ``` On Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, install the prerequisites and run the Linux installer: ```bash sudo apt install curl ca-certificates tar unzip coreutils findutils gawk grep diffutils procps util-linux systemd python3 tesseract-ocr tesseract-ocr-eng poppler-utils libvips-tools libheif1 ffmpeg curl -fsSL https://olympusplugin.ai/install-linux.sh | sh ``` Each installer installs Olympus for your user only (the installer itself needs no administrator password; the package installation lines above do), checks every download against a pinned SHA-256 before using it, keeps Olympus running in the background (a LaunchAgent on a Mac, a systemd user service on Linux), adds the `olympus` command, and waits until the engine proves it is running. On Omarchy it also adds **Olympus** to the app launcher. Then Olympus downloads its built-in models once. Running it again updates or repairs the install; a failed update puts the previous version back. Details, folders and uninstall: . **2. Connect your AI.** Each app has a short guide: [ChatGPT](https://olympusplugin.ai/install/chatgpt/) · [Claude](https://olympusplugin.ai/install/claude/) · [Grok and Grok Bot](https://olympusplugin.ai/install/grok/) · [Dots](https://olympusplugin.ai/install/dots/) · [Claude Code](https://olympusplugin.ai/install/claude-code/) · [Codex](https://olympusplugin.ai/install/codex/) · [OpenClaw](https://olympusplugin.ai/install/openclaw/) · [Hermes](https://olympusplugin.ai/install/hermes/) · [any MCP app](https://olympusplugin.ai/install/other/). In ChatGPT, Claude and Grok you add Olympus's address as a connector (in ChatGPT, in Developer mode until Olympus is listed in its directory), then approve it with one click on a page Olympus opens on your own computer: there is no pairing code and no account to create. Grok Bot then uses the Grok connection. Apps on your computer, such as Claude Code, Codex and Hermes, connect with one command. **3. Connect your sources and ask.** Open the dashboard (in ChatGPT, ask *"Show my Olympus dashboard"*; on your computer, run `olympus dashboard`), connect Dropbox, Gmail or Google Drive, pick folders, and ask the way you normally would. ## Olympus for ChatGPT In ChatGPT, Olympus is a plugin. The Olympus engine runs on your computer and keeps your index there; ChatGPT asks it questions through one secure connection that you approve on that computer. ### 1. Add Olympus in ChatGPT Install Olympus on your computer first ([Get started](#get-started)). Olympus is on its way to ChatGPT's app directory. Until it is listed, add it yourself: in ChatGPT, open **Plugins**, choose **+**, then **Add custom MCP server**. Name it Olympus, choose OAuth, and paste `https://mcp.olympusplugin.ai/mcp` as the URL. If you don't see Add custom MCP server, turn on **Developer mode** in **Settings** first. OpenAI decides which accounts have Developer mode; in a work or school workspace, an admin may need to allow it. Step by step: . On Omarchy, ChatGPT may still say Olympus needs a Mac; it works on Omarchy too. ### 2. Approve ChatGPT on your computer The first time ChatGPT connects to Olympus, an Olympus page opens in your computer's browser asking *Connect ChatGPT to Olympus?* Click **Connect**. (If a page saying *Approve ChatGPT on your Mac* comes first, click **Continue on this Mac**; the page says Mac on Omarchy too.) Clicking Connect on your own computer is how Olympus knows the computer is yours: there is no code to copy and no account to create. To check on it later, run `olympus engine status` in a terminal. ### 3. Connect Dropbox and choose folders Open the **Olympus** dashboard in ChatGPT's sidebar (or ask *"Show my Olympus dashboard"*). Choose **Connect** next to Dropbox and sign in with your own Dropbox account; the sign-in link works once, for 10 minutes, from any device. Gmail and Google Drive connect the same way, except that you open their sign-in link on the computer where Olympus runs, not on a phone. Then pick folders. For each folder choose: - **Full**: Olympus reads the files and can answer from what they say. - **Names only**: Olympus keeps the file names and details such as dates, not what the files say. - **Skip**: Olympus leaves the folder alone. A folder follows its parent's choice unless you change it; **Mixed** means some folders inside it are set differently. Choose **Save and start**, and indexing begins on your computer. ### 4. Tell Olympus what's private Olympus sorts every item, one by one, into one of three tiers: - **Personal**: everyday mail, notes and files. ChatGPT can see the parts that answer your question, and cites them. - **Private**: things you keep to yourself, such as health, money or family matters. What they say is never sent to ChatGPT. Olympus answers from them on your computer, in the private answer panel (below). - **Secret**: passwords, recovery codes and keys. What Olympus recognizes as a Secret never reaches a model and is never answered from. Recognition looks for common forms (private keys, API keys, labeled passwords) and can miss others. Olympus decides on your computer. Once its built-in private model is ready, it checks every item it reads before treating it as Personal. Labels are automatic and can be wrong. In the dashboard, **Privacy** asks *"What's private for you?"*: answer in your own words. Once you do, only the kinds of things you call private are Private: health or family matters you leave out, or say are fine to share, can reach ChatGPT. You can also mark folders, Gmail labels or senders as always Private. ### 5. Ask Ask in ChatGPT the way you normally would: *"What did Sam say about the lease?"* ChatGPT searches Olympus and answers from your Personal items, with citations. Olympus also scores search matches with a built-in reranker on computers with 16 GB of memory or more (16 GiB measured RAM). Scoring runs only on this computer. Installing the search model adds one reranker download of about 136 MB; answers use the fused keyword and vector order until it is installed. The reranker is released after 10 idle minutes and loads again when needed. Set `OLYMPUS_SOURCE_RERANKER=off` to turn it off, or `built-in` to enable it on a computer with less memory. ### The private answer panel When some of the items that match your question are Private, a small Olympus panel appears on its own under ChatGPT's reply: **Private answer from your computer**, marked **Not sent to ChatGPT**. - Your computer writes the answer with its built-in private model (Qwen3.5, sized to its memory: 2B under 16 GB, 4B with more) and sends it to the panel sealed, so only the panel can open it. It goes around the ChatGPT conversation, not through it, and the Olympus relay cannot read it. - On an Apple silicon Mac it usually arrives within a minute; on Omarchy it depends on the computer's processor and can take a few minutes. Ask for *"all the details"* and Olympus reads the whole documents instead; that can take a few minutes. - **Sources** (closed at first) lists the items the answer used. Click one to open it on your computer, or in Dropbox on the web if it is not on this computer (ChatGPT opens that web link for you, so it sees the address). - **Hide** folds the answer away and **Show** brings it back. An answer expires after 10 minutes; ask again for a new one. - Ask follow-up questions in the chat as usual; each private answer appears in a new panel. Your computer needs to be awake and online. The panel runs inside ChatGPT's page, so it relies on the panel code ChatGPT loads; the [design](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/docs/design/chatgpt-plugin.md#who-can-read-the-answer) states that limit plainly. ### What ChatGPT can and can't see ChatGPT **can** see: - The parts of your Personal items that answer a question: excerpts, titles, dates and links. - File names, including the names of some Private items. A file's name can be Personal while what it says is Private, so its name may show up in ChatGPT; its contents never do. - That some items matching a question are Private: ChatGPT's model learns just that, with no titles and no content. - Status: which sources are connected, how far indexing has got, and what needs you. The folder picker shows your folder names inside ChatGPT so you can choose; they pass through ChatGPT to reach the picker, but ChatGPT's model is not given them. ChatGPT **can't** see: - What your Private items say, or the private answers made from them. - Secret items Olympus recognizes. - Folders you skip, or what the files in Names-only folders say. - API keys or passwords: you never enter one in ChatGPT. Optional extras such as a Venice account are set up on your computer. The relay at `mcp.olympusplugin.ai` passes ChatGPT's requests to your computer. It stores and logs no questions, answers or tokens, but like any HTTPS service it handles them in transit. Full details: the [ChatGPT design](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/docs/design/chatgpt-plugin.md) and the [trust model](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/docs/TRUST_MODEL.md). ## Claude, Grok and other apps Claude (web, desktop and phone) and Grok connect through the same Olympus relay as ChatGPT, with one click to approve on your computer, and Grok Bot uses the Grok connection; apps on your computer, such as Claude Code, Codex and Hermes, connect there directly. Guides: . They search what is Personal, with citations, like ChatGPT. They never get your Private items themselves or the Secrets Olympus recognizes. For Private items they get at most an answer that the private model on your computer (or Venice, if you set it up) writes from them, checked for secrets, with each item's title, path, source and author. That answer can repeat what the items say. ChatGPT is stricter: it gets no answer from Private items at all, and shows one only in its private answer panel. When an agent is not given an answer, Olympus records the question and the model built into Olympus answers it on your computer; the agent is told only that the answer is in Olympus on your computer, with a link (`olympus://open/private/` and a random identifier) that opens it there. The answer waits in the dashboard's [Inbox](https://olympusplugin.ai/open/private/) (under **On this computer**), which Olympus gives no AI app a way to read, until you delete it, and **Needs you** counts the answers you have not read. More: [Connect other agents](#connect-other-agents). ## Stronger models, privately For hard private questions you can reach stronger models without giving yourself away. Both are off until you turn them on. - **[Venice](https://venice.ai)** runs private models that, under Venice's own terms, keep nothing you send. Add your Venice key under **Keys**, on your computer. In **Ask a question**, a Venice model reads the passages of your files it needs, and is available only if your privacy settings allow Private items to go to Venice; a key alone does not allow it. - **zkAPI**, from OpenAnonymity and the Ethereum Foundation, hides who is asking. It pays anonymously and sends the question over Tor (on unless you turn it off; without Tor, your network address shows): no account, no card, no name, just proof the question is paid for. In **Strict** mode your computer first rewrites the question into general questions; **Standard**, by default, takes out names, contact details and account numbers, or sends your words as written if you choose that. What you ask can still identify you. Turn on **Anonymous answers** under **Keys** on your computer, then ask from your agent or from **Ask a question** in the dashboard's [Inbox](https://olympusplugin.ai/open/private/); each question as sent, and its reply, stay in the Inbox on your computer until you delete them or the Inbox removes the oldest when full. Anonymous answers work on a Mac and on Omarchy and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (x64), once Olympus's network isolation checks pass. ## Uninstall On a Mac, run `curl -fsSL https://olympusplugin.ai/uninstall.sh | sh`; on Linux, `curl -fsSL https://olympusplugin.ai/uninstall-linux.sh | sh`. Both stop Olympus and remove the app, the runtime and the `olympus` command, and keep your settings and data. To delete those too, first run `olympus engine stop` and `olympus data delete --all`. To only stop Olympus and remove its login item or service, run `olympus engine uninstall`. The rest of this README covers how Olympus works and Olympus with OpenClaw, which stays supported and optional. ## How it works Olympus ingests your sources into local, trust-tiered indexes, then lets your frontier agent answer questions across all of them, with sensitive material handled only by lanes you approved: your own local models, privacy-approved private cloud inference, or not at all. Every item you ingest is judged on its own as Personal, Private, or Secrets (plus Public on installs made before 1.0; internally S0-S5): its names are Personal unless something raises them, and its content is raised to Private or Secrets on evidence. Each tier has its own index and routes only to the model lanes your sovereignty policy allows: ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph sources["Your sources"] direction TB SRC1[Gmail · Drive · Dropbox] SRC2[Telegram · WhatsApp · X] end subgraph olympus["Olympus (local)"] direction TB ING[Ingest & classify
every item, locally] IDX[(Trust-tiered
local indexes)] POL{{Sovereignty policy
your rules, enforced}} ING --> IDX --> POL end subgraph lanes["Model lanes you approved"] direction TB CLOUD[Frontier cloud
everyday content] PRIVATE[Venice
Private content when routed] LOCAL[Your local models
Private content] end AGENT[Your agent
cited, bounded answers] sources --> ING POL --> CLOUD & PRIVATE & LOCAL CLOUD & PRIVATE & LOCAL --> AGENT ``` Olympus uses **Personal** (ordinary personal and work content), **Private** (sensitive material), and **Secrets** (once recognized, never model input). There is no Public tier on any new install, ChatGPT or OpenClaw, whichever posture you choose: anything that would have been Public is Personal. Installs made before 1.0 keep a **Public** tier. See the [tier mapping](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/docs/TRUST_MODEL.md#product-tier-names) for the unchanged storage identifiers. Four postures, chosen (and changeable) in setup — a config file, not a code fork: | Preset | Personal content | Private content: health, finance, legal, therapy, family | |---|---|---| | **Local models and private cloud** (`local-first`) | frontier cloud | approved secure pool with explicit local → [Venice](https://venice.ai) Private order | | **Local models only** (`local-only`) | frontier cloud | your own local models only | | **Private cloud only** (`private-cloud-only`) | frontier cloud | [Venice](https://venice.ai) Private model (`kimi-k3`) | | **Private meaning search on this computer** (`no-sensitive`) | frontier cloud | **stored and searched by meaning on this computer**: its search vectors come from the built-in model and are kept here; no Private agent answer lane | The engine sizes local answer prompts from the model's served context window when it can read it at startup (or the built-in model's manifest). Unknown windows keep the 13,500-byte fallback. Automatic sizing reserves answer tokens and framing space and caps prompts at 27,000 bytes, the size that kept every passage hit in measurement. `/health` lists each local answer route's `local_prompt_budget` source, so a fallback shows. `OLYMPUS_SOURCE_INDEX_LOCAL_ANALYST_PROMPT_BYTES` still overrides that size. “Private cloud only” describes **Private-data handling**: Venice answers Private questions. Search indexing for every tier uses EmbeddingGemma 2, Google's small embedding model, built into Olympus: it downloads once, runs on your computer, needs no account or key, and sends nothing anywhere. On a Mac it also reads pictures, so photos are searchable by what is in them. The embedding choices are built-in local EmbeddingGemma or Venice. Existing Gemini and local-server configurations remain compatible; see the [embedding migration guide](docs/SOVEREIGNTY_CONFIG.md#legacy-embedding-migration). Private content never goes to Gemini. Personal questions use OpenClaw's own configured default model. One question searches every tier. When it finds Private evidence, the private lane your posture approved answers it and your agent receives only the checked, cited answer. Secrets Olympus recognizes are never searched by content: it can tell you where one lives, never what it says. Some rules are not configurable, by design: secure content never routes to ordinary cloud models, recognized secrets are denied to every lane, and an exhausted policy chain refuses rather than silently downgrading. ## Get started with OpenClaw Using ChatGPT? See [Olympus for ChatGPT](#olympus-for-chatgpt) instead; none of this section is needed. **You need** OpenClaw `2026.7.1+` on a Node release OpenClaw itself supports (`>=24.16.0 <25` or `>=26.1.0` for OpenClaw 2026.9.5; check `npm view openclaw engines` — its installer refuses any other), plus [Bun](https://bun.sh) `1.2+`. macOS or Linux. Paste this into OpenClaw, or another agent with a terminal: > Install Olympus by reading https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/main/INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md and following it step by step. Walk me through setup and ask me about my data and privacy preferences. Your agent downloads the designated pilot package, checks it automatically, and guides you through setup. You do not need to download files, find a checksum receipt, or have a GitHub account. The agent checks the SHA-256 and byte count against the designated candidate and GitHub's release metadata. Olympus is also published on ClawHub (https://clawhub.ai/plugins/olympus, from 1.3.4), so `openclaw plugins install clawhub:olympus` installs the same release bytes. ClawHub can trail the newest GitHub release by a little. The agent install above and release qualification use the managed `npm-pack:` path — see [docs/V0_4_RELEASE.md](docs/V0_4_RELEASE.md). A Git checkout or rebuilt package does not qualify the supplied candidate. `--accept-capabilities` is required by OpenClaw `2026.8.1+`: an agent-driven install is non-TTY, and without the flag the host exits 1 asking for capability consent it cannot prompt for. Omit the flag on `2026.7.1`, which does not define it. The agent checks prerequisites, installs the plugin, talks through what is private for you (you save it later in the dashboard's Privacy section), asks for your privacy posture and your approval of the private classifier, verifies the worker, restarts the gateway, and hands you the dashboard. You paste your model keys into its **Models** section yourself; the agent never collects them. That completes base installation. Then you can choose a source in the dashboard or leave Olympus ready for later; no source is selected for you. Once your chosen source is ready, the agent checks a first answer and its citations. Prefer to drive it yourself? Follow **[docs/QUICKSTART.md](docs/QUICKSTART.md)**, starting with the automatic download and existing-install checks. Its install command for a clean machine is: ```bash openclaw plugins install npm-pack:/absolute/path/to/olympus-1.4.4.tgz --force --accept-capabilities # On OpenClaw 2026.7.1, omit both flags for a clean install. # On newer hosts, --force also overwrites an existing plugin: check first. openclaw plugins enable olympus OLYMPUS_ROOT="$(openclaw plugins inspect olympus --json | jq -r .plugin.rootDir)" OLYMPUS_BIN="$OLYMPUS_ROOT/bin/olympus" "$OLYMPUS_BIN" doctor ``` Continue the quickstart to describe your data, choose a privacy posture, connect model credentials, and verify base activation before choosing your sources in the dashboard and checking the first cited answer. Setup installs an owner-only `~/.local/bin/olympus` launcher on Linux and macOS and keeps it aligned with worker upgrades and rollback. Existing user or standalone launchers are preserved. If `~/.local/bin` is missing from your login PATH, run `"$HOME/.local/bin/olympus" dashboard` on the machine running Olympus (on a server, use that server). Setup reports the full command, including a fallback when an existing launcher belongs to another installer. This candidate artifact includes native Control UI support. On OpenClaw **2026.9.2**, use **Olympus** in the Control UI sidebar to connect sources, choose scope, and follow ingestion. Enable **Settings → Labs → Custom plugin UI** (the Gateway restarts itself to apply it on OpenClaw 2026.9.5; run no second restart), then reload the browser. OpenClaw currently makes this integration experimental and requires its own Gateway's Control UI over HTTPS or localhost. Olympus uses your signed-in OpenClaw permissions; its worker token stays on the server. The standalone `olympus dashboard` command remains available for older hosts, when custom plugin UI is off, and for direct access when needed. See the [dashboard guide](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/docs/QUICKSTART.md#5-open-your-dashboard-and-connect-sources). For Venice embeddings, Venice accounts/API credit, local answer models, or legacy embedding migration, use the [agent-led model setup guide](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/docs/SOVEREIGNTY_CONFIG.md#agent-led-model-setup-for-the-v04-beta). It explains the separate Private and Personal routes, registered embedding defaults, and custom-model requirements before you connect keys or restart. In the dashboard you paste each key into its **Models** card. For a headless setup, choose how to supply each key: paste it yourself from your password manager's website into the silent terminal input, or authorize an exact named-item read through an already authenticated manager CLI. The manual route needs no password-manager desktop app or CLI; a 1Password `op://` reference needs authenticated `op` access for an agent fetch. On OpenClaw `2026.9.2`, use Olympus in the Control UI sidebar when the installed Olympus artifact includes native Control UI support and Custom plugin UI is enabled. Host version alone is not proof of support. Otherwise the quickstart uses the retained standalone dashboard; it explains the different authentication requirements for each route. ## Supported sources | Source | Connect flow | Notes | |---|---|---| | Gmail | browser OAuth | Spam and Trash left out | | Google Drive | browser OAuth | docs + files | | Dropbox | browser OAuth | full file spine: metadata, extraction, OCR, audio transcribed on your machine | | Files on this computer | choose folders | no account; nothing is chosen by default | | Archives | choose an export file | mbox mail, WhatsApp chat export, Telegram Desktop JSON, Reflect, Roam, Evernote .enex; read where it is | | Evernote | sign in with Evernote | read permission only; you choose the notebooks | | Telegram | guided phone login | forward sync of active chats | | WhatsApp | QR pairing | live bridge | | X bookmarks | browser OAuth with a user-owned developer app | folder provenance and provider cost ceilings | | Readwise | API key | optional | Olympus supports one connected account per provider. The full capability list (scopes, dependencies, provider limits, formats) is generated from the public roster in [docs/SOURCE_CAPABILITIES.md](docs/SOURCE_CAPABILITIES.md). Model-lane credentials such as Venice are privacy-mode prerequisites, not sources. Tokens live in an encrypted local secret store by default, or in an explicitly configured OS secret store when supported, never in plain text. Ingestion, classification, and indexing all run in one supervised local worker — `olympus worker install` makes it start on login. Every source syncs through the same connector-store runtime. After setup, the dashboard guides the source you choose from sign-in and scope through the first sync to cited answers, and shows the next step for a source that is blocked or degraded. You connect only the sources you want. On an existing live OpenClaw install, treat plugin install/enable, gateway restart, worker service changes, and plugin refresh as live-system changes: validate with `openclaw config validate` and `openclaw doctor --lint`, then restart only through `openclaw gateway restart` or the documented ops refresh script. The repo docs and commands should never require raw edits to OpenClaw runtime config. ## The security model Olympus is built on the assumption that the boundary *is* the product: - **Local-first ingestion.** Raw source content lands in local SQLite indexes before any model sees anything. Classification happens on your computer unless you choose Venice for it. - **Sanitized handoffs.** Agents receive answer text, excerpts of Personal items, citations, and audit counts — typed wire shapes with `raw_source_exposed: false`, re-validated client-side. Embeddings, cursors, and tokens never cross. Private items reach an agent only as answers written from them, which can repeat what they say; ChatGPT's model gets none. - **A hard membrane.** Any evidence pack containing sensitive material is barred from standard cloud lanes by two independent checks — policy validation at config load, and a runtime re-check on every request. - **Fail closed, everywhere.** No approved lane for a tier means a refusal with an honest error — never a silent fallback to a less-trusted model. - **Authenticated by default.** The worker binds loopback with bearer-token auth on every route; new installs generate the token during setup. Browser controls exchange it for a short-lived HttpOnly local session protected by same-origin and CSRF checks; the bearer is never stored by the page. - **A real exit.** `olympus data export` gives you your data; `olympus data delete --all` verifiably removes indexes, embeddings, configs, tokens, and service units. The onboarding flow, end to end: ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Install
plugin] --> B[olympus setup
pick your posture] B --> C[olympus connect
OAuth IDs · session paths · API-key stdin] C --> D[Dashboard
watch it ingest] D --> E[Ask your agent
cited answers] ``` ## Command reference | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `olympus setup --preset --yes` | writes sovereignty policy and worker auth for the chosen posture | | `olympus connect ...` | records OAuth, session, or API-key credentials with source-specific flags | | `olympus worker foreground\|install\|start\|stop\|restart\|status\|upgrade\|uninstall` | one versioned lifecycle for the local engine, foreground or supervised | | `olympus dashboard` | opens the standalone dashboard with a short-lived authorization link; no worker-token copying | | `olympus dashboard --no-open` | generates an unused opening link for an agent to hand to you | | `olympus dashboard token` | advanced compatibility access to the worker bearer; never share it in chat | | `olympus source answer "…"` | ask across your sources from the terminal | | `olympus ask "…" [--level strict\|standard]` | one question to a frontier model anonymously through zkAPI (paid from your zkAPI balance; the question only) | | `olympus archive start --path \|status\|remove --archive-id ` | asks to import an old export (such as a mail `.mbox`) or to remove an imported one; you approve on the dashboard, and `status` shows progress without any message text | | `olympus tier explain\|set\|recheck\|rules\|classifier …` | why an item has its tier, owner overrides, checking one chat's or source's privacy again, rules, and the private classifier's approval | | `olympus tier migrate plan\|approve\|run\|rollback\|purge\|status` | moves an existing install's items into per-item tiers, each step owner-approved after a dry-run plan | | `olympus doctor` | diagnoses problems, each with a fix-it hint | | `olympus data export\|delete` | your data, out — or gone | | `olympus serve` | MCP stdio server for non-OpenClaw agents | `olympus worker install` and `upgrade` atomically reconcile the generated service unit and owner-only worker environment before activation. Interrupted install or upgrade transactions recover the previous managed files when the same command is rerun. `status` reports the observed service and transaction state; it never guesses that an unreadable manager or non-regular managed path is healthy. `uninstall` removes only the supervised service and intentionally retains credentials, source configuration, and indexed data. Use the separate data lifecycle when those bytes should also be removed. Credential, scope, pairing, Disconnect, partial-sync, and source-dependency repairs do not normally require a worker restart. Follow the source card or `olympus doctor` recovery action instead. Dashboard **Disconnect** stops new scheduled and manual reads, removes the selected local account grant, and keeps indexed data and reusable developer-app registration. It does not revoke provider-side access; the card links the provider revocation page. Local data deletion remains the deliberate CLI-only flow: preview `olympus data delete --source --dry-run`, Disconnect the source, then run the command without `--dry-run`. Telegram and WhatsApp are paired sessions rather than broker grants, so their cards carry **Unpair** instead: it stops new reads and deletes this computer's pairing session, keeping indexed messages and captured media, and leaves the linked device in place at the provider for you to remove there. ### Connect other agents Open the dashboard on this computer (`olympus dashboard`). Under **On this computer**, choose **Open** next to **Agents**, then press **Connect an agent**. Pick the agent you use and follow its steps; every address and snippet has a copy button. - **ChatGPT**: add Olympus in ChatGPT (Developer mode until it is listed; see [Olympus for ChatGPT](#olympus-for-chatgpt)), then click **Connect** on the page that opens in this computer's browser. - **Claude Code** and **Codex** on this computer: copy the prompt (or the `olympus serve` command) into the agent. This works without remote access. - **Claude** (web, desktop and phone) and **Grok** (grok.com): add Olympus as a connector with the address the panel shows, then click **Connect** on the page that opens in this computer's browser. - **Grok Bot**: nothing to add. Once Olympus is connected on grok.com, Grok Bot uses that connection, with the same xAI account. - **Agent on another account of this computer**: for OpenClaw, Hermes or an MCP client running under another account. Name the agent and choose **Create key**, then copy its setup line into the agent. It connects to this computer only, without reading your Olympus files or signing in. - **Agent on my tailnet**: for an agent on your Tailscale network. Keep Tailscale running on both computers, then create a key and copy the setup line. If Tailscale is not running here, the page says so. - The **Grok API** and other agents in the cloud need a tunnel you run yourself (below), unless the agent can use one of the private choices above. The private choices use a different key for each named agent. Each address starts listening only while it has an active key; revoking its last key stops it. The connection list shows which route each key uses. Keys and setup lines are shown once, so copy them before choosing **Done**. These connections use the same remote tools and privacy rules as the relay, with no question limits. They work independently of the remote access switch. Agents in the cloud reach Olympus only when remote access is on; the Agents page says whether it is. To turn it on, press **Turn on remote access** there. Olympus then connects through the Olympus relay (`mcp.olympusplugin.ai`): you create no account and run no tunnel. The relay passes requests between your agents and this computer; it stores and logs no questions, answers or tokens, but like any HTTPS endpoint it handles them in transit. The relay connects ChatGPT, Claude, Grok (grok.com) and Grok Bot, and approving one happens on this computer only, with one click on a page Olympus serves locally; there is no pairing code. A Claude connector approved on this computer then works in Claude on your phone too. **Turn off remote access** turns it off again. If the relay cannot be reached, the page says **Olympus relay unavailable** and Olympus keeps retrying on its own; agents on this computer are unaffected. Advanced: to use a tunnel you run yourself instead of the relay, set `plugins.entries.olympus.config.remote.publicBaseUrl` to its https origin (`openclaw config set …`) and turn remote access on. Through your own tunnel, Claude, ChatGPT and Grok approve Olympus on its approval page with a one-time pairing code from the Agents page, and the Grok API takes an address plus a key from **Create key** (shown once). Every connected agent gets the same privacy rules as your OpenClaw agent. It never gets Private items themselves or the Secrets Olympus recognizes. For Private items it receives only answers that Venice or a local model wrote from them, which can repeat what they say, with each item's title, path, source and author. The Agents page lists connected agents with when each was added and last used, and **Revoke** removes one. `olympus connections list|revoke|pair|add` does the same from a terminal. Each agent's steps end with a short instruction that tells it when to ask Olympus. Paste it into Claude project instructions, Grok's custom instructions or Grok Bot's skills, or load the packaged Agent Skills folder [`integrations/agent-skills/ask-olympus/`](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/integrations/agent-skills/ask-olympus/SKILL.md). ### Using Olympus from other agents (MCP) `olympus serve` exposes the same sanitized read operations — `source_answer`, `source_answer_result`, `source_index_status`, capability-gated `source_index_search`, `ask_anonymously`, `archive_import`, `privacy_item_find` and `privacy_item_set` — to any MCP-capable agent. The supported Hermes configuration narrows that server to exactly `source_answer`, `source_answer_result`, `source_index_status` and `ask_anonymously` through its per-server tool allowlist. `archive_import` (start, status, remove) lets an agent ask to import an old export the user wants searched, such as a mail `.mbox` from Google Takeout or Apple Mail. It only asks: `start` stores the path as text without opening it and returns `needs_approval`; the user approves on the Olympus dashboard on their computer (Sources, Archives), and `remove` works the same way. `status` reports each archive's progress, counts, date range and gaps, never message text. It is on the native, MCP and CLI surfaces only, not on Hermes, remote MCP or the ChatGPT relay. `privacy_item_find` and `privacy_item_set` let an agent act on "that email should be private": find the item by words from its title, sender or file name (items whose names are Private, and Secret items, are never listed), then make it Private. That is the user's decision on that one item, never a rule for its sender, chat or folder. An agent can only raise an item: making it Personal, or putting it back to the judge's label, is the user's on their own computer (`olympus tier set`). Same surfaces as `archive_import`. `ask_anonymously` sends one typed question to a frontier model through zkAPI (paid per question, anonymously, from the user's own balance; what the question says can still identify them). The first call with no `level` returns `needs_choice`: the agent asks the user once for Strict (their own model rewrites the question into general questions before it leaves) or Standard (their words, prepared as written, lightly cleaned up or by their saved instruction), then calls again with `level` and `remember: true`. Only the question goes out, never documents, and never to the provider that hosts the agent asking: a question from ChatGPT goes to Claude Sonnet by default, one from Claude Code or Claude Desktop to an OpenAI model, and a one-off `model` from the agent's own provider is refused. Setup (the zkAPI route, the writer model, the zkAPI models for questions from ChatGPT and from Claude, the spend limit) lives on the dashboard's Anonymous answers card, under Keys. Questions are asked through an agent, `olympus ask`, or **Ask a question** in the dashboard's Inbox; each question as sent, and its reply, are kept in the Inbox on your computer until you delete them or the Inbox removes the oldest when full. See [`docs/design/private-answers.md`](docs/design/private-answers.md). MCP clients cap how long one tool call may run, and an answer can take several minutes. So over MCP (local `olympus serve` and remote `/mcp` alike) and the OpenAPI tool paths, a `source_answer` that is not done by a hand-off threshold returns `{"status": "working", "job_id": …}` and keeps running. The threshold is 45 seconds for remote agents (`OLYMPUS_SOURCE_ANSWER_HANDOFF_MS`, under the MCP SDK's 60-second default request timeout) and for local `olympus serve` (`OLYMPUS_SOURCE_ANSWER_STDIO_HANDOFF_MS`, under Codex's 60-second default tool timeout); both are capped at 230000. `source_answer_result` with that `job_id` returns the answer, the same error the call would have raised, or `working` again after waiting up to a minute (never longer than the threshold). A slow `ask_anonymously` (a Tor route can take minutes) hands off the same way and is collected with the same tool. A job that runs past 20 minutes is stopped with `source_answer_deadline`, and revoking a connection drops its jobs. Remote answers share the analyst with your own assistant's answers; there is no priority lane. So the worker runs at most two remote answers at once (the analyst's lane count; `OLYMPUS_SOURCE_ANSWER_MAX_RUNNING` raises it for a multi-lane analyst) and refuses more with `source_answer_busy`, which bounds how much remote work can ever queue ahead of your own question. A caller that disconnects, or a job that reaches its deadline, stops the analyst call itself and frees the lane. A job id is readable only by the connection (or `olympus serve` process) that asked, lives in memory, and expires 15 minutes after its answer is ready. For Hermes Agent, resolve the installed plugin first: ```bash openclaw plugins inspect olympus --json ``` Copy `plugin.rootDir` from that content-free response, append `/bin/olympus`, and pass the resulting absolute executable path to Hermes: ```bash hermes mcp add olympus --command /absolute/managed/olympus/bin/olympus --args serve hermes mcp test olympus ``` Make the `olympus` server entry in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` match the packaged [`config/hermes/olympus.mcp.yaml`](config/hermes/olympus.mcp.yaml): ```yaml mcp_servers: olympus: command: /bin/olympus args: [serve] tools: include: [source_answer, source_answer_result, source_index_status, ask_anonymously] prompts: false resources: false ``` Restart Hermes or run `/reload-mcp`, then verify that the discovered registered names are exactly `mcp_olympus_source_answer`, `mcp_olympus_source_answer_result`, `mcp_olympus_source_index_status` and `mcp_olympus_ask_anonymously`. Invoke the discovered names rather than hard-coding them. A cited-answer round trip uses the discovered `mcp_olympus_source_answer`; `source_watch_*` remains OpenClaw-only. The optional packaged Hermes skill is [`integrations/hermes/ask-sources/SKILL.md`](integrations/hermes/ask-sources/SKILL.md). It is also published on ClawHub, which Hermes's skills hub searches, so `hermes skills install clawhub/olympus-hermes` installs it. Or copy its directory to `~/.hermes/skills/ask-sources/` or expose the parent with `skills.external_dirs`; it declares the same four tools and no fallback access. No `hermes://mcp/install` link is published: current Hermes upstream documents custom MCP installation through `hermes mcp add` but does not document that URI handler. There are no operator agent tools. Index maintenance — sync, extraction, embedding, retries — is the worker's own scheduler, and what a person drives by hand goes through the `olympus` CLI. The whole agent tool surface is sixteen tools — `argus_ping`, `argus_list_models`, `argus_complete`, `source_answer`, `source_answer_result` (MCP and remote only), `source_index_status`, `source_index_search`, `source_watch_create`, `source_watches`, `source_watch_cancel`, `olympus_doctor`, `olympus_setup_status`, `ask_anonymously`, `archive_import`, `privacy_item_find`, `privacy_item_set` — declared in [`src/core/public-surface.ts`](src/core/public-surface.ts); Hermes over MCP sees the subset above, and worker bearer auth is enforced throughout. Operational note for connector-store corpora: a source with an account folder (Gmail, Drive, Dropbox, local files, Readwise, X, Telegram, WhatsApp, imported archives) keeps its stores where Olympus places them, and its `OLYMPUS_SOURCE_INDEX_CONNECTOR_STORES_JSON` entry names no path: it only adds a principal to the store its lane opened. A store only the mount list places (Reflect, Roam) is mounted with the same corpus id, `family`, `trustDomain` and `dbPath` its sync script writes, and that corpus id must be in the corpus registry — a store mounted for an unregistered corpus fills but is never read. Chat-family mounts must also declare their exact principal identity with `principalProvider` and `principalAccountScope` (for example, `whatsapp` and `personal`). Structured scopes use the stored account scope as their prefix, so the shipped WhatsApp identity is `personal:chat:` while Telegram remains `telegram.personal:chat:`. A chat mount without both fields remains available for non-`chat_scope` reads, but `chat_scope` filtering fails closed as not configured; mounted rows never establish account authority. The migration-era indexes, replay/import utilities, read-authority switches, and retired store writers were removed in Slice 2. Canonical connector stores are now the only source read/write authority. Compatibility aliases that remain at input boundaries do not select another runtime or store. ## Development Olympus is TypeScript on Bun: one plugin package, stable versioned architecture contracts (`SourceConnector` / `EvidencePack` / `Analyst` — only the connector is per-source), and 3,400+ tests including an architecture guard that keeps per-source answer logic out of the shared spine. ```bash bun install bun run test:focus -- test/example.test.ts ``` Use focused local proof while editing; GitHub requires each substantive CI lane and runs the complete suite in parallel before merge. See the canonical [engineering process](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/docs/ENGINEERING_PROCESS.md). Deep-dive docs: [contracts and architecture](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/docs/CONTRACTS.md) · [trust model](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/docs/TRUST_MODEL.md) · [sovereignty config](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/docs/SOVEREIGNTY_CONFIG.md) · [uninstall](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/docs/UNINSTALL.md) ## License [MIT](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/LICENSE) — free for any use, including commercial. Olympus is provided as is, without warranty; keep your own backups. Olympus is published by Open Coordination Unlimited, Inc. Its hosted relay is governed by the [Terms of Service](https://olympusplugin.ai/terms/) and [Privacy Policy](https://olympusplugin.ai/privacy/). Third-party data notices: [docs/THIRD_PARTY_DATA.md](docs/THIRD_PARTY_DATA.md). Want to suggest a change? See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): fork, branch, open a PR. Read access doesn't include direct pushes — everything lands through review.
