When an update is available, the app shows an update indicator; supported platforms can also install from Settings → General. ### First run Local mode is the default: launch the app and it starts tracking this device. No hub, agent, or config required. ## Multi-device sync Pick ONE multi-device sync backend for your devices (and any headless agents). On each device, open the widget and pick a mode under Settings → Multi-device Sync. The widget contributes this device's usage automatically; run the [headless agent](#headless-agent) only on machines without a widget. iCloud Drive is a macOS-widget-only option and does not support headless agents. #### Option A — Host the hub from the widget (easiest, no CLI) In the widget on one always-on machine, open Settings → Multi-device Sync and pick **Host hub on this device**. The widget generates a random secret and lists the LAN URLs other devices can connect to (Tailscale or ZeroTier addresses appear here too). On every other device, pick **Connect to a hub** and paste the URL + secret. The hub runs while Token Monitor is running — quitting (not just closing the window) stops it for all connected devices. #### Option B — Self-hosted Node hub (always-on headless machine) ```bash # on the always-on machine cp .env.example .env # set TOKEN_MONITOR_SECRET to something private, then: npm run hub ``` #### Option C — Cloudflare Worker hub (across networks, including iPhone) [![Deploy to Cloudflare](https://deploy.workers.cloudflare.com/button)](https://deploy.workers.cloudflare.com/?url=https://github.com/Javis603/token-monitor/tree/main/worker) One-click deploy — Cloudflare will prompt for the `TOKEN_MONITOR_SECRET` during setup. Or deploy manually: ```bash cd worker npm install npx wrangler login npx wrangler secret put TOKEN_MONITOR_SECRET npx wrangler deploy ``` Paste the deployed URL into each device's widget at Settings → Multi-device Sync. See [worker/README.md](worker/README.md) for the iOS widget recipe and endpoint reference, or [docs/API.md](docs/API.md) for the hub HTTP API. #### Option D — iCloud Drive (macOS, no Hub server) On each Mac signed into the same Apple ID, choose **iCloud Drive** in Settings → Multi-device Sync. This is an opt-in macOS-only path: Token Monitor writes one atomic snapshot per device and one subscription snapshot per writer under `iCloud Drive/Token Monitor/sync-v1/`, then each Mac aggregates the valid files locally. It uses no Token Monitor server, CloudKit, or credentials; provider API keys, cookies, and tokens stay local. iCloud Drive is eventually consistent, so another Mac may take a moment to appear or update, and a missing or malformed file never clears the last-good aggregate. ### Headless agent Run the headless agent on servers, SSH hosts, or inside WSL — anywhere you use AI tools without the desktop widget. It collects usage on that machine and posts it to your hub (Option A, B, or C). Requires Node.js 22.15+ and git. ```bash git clone https://github.com/Javis603/token-monitor.git cd token-monitor npm ci cp .env.example .env # set TOKEN_MONITOR_HUB_URL, TOKEN_MONITOR_SECRET, and a unique TOKEN_MONITOR_DEVICE_ID npm run agent # run continuously ``` See [docs/headless-agent.md](docs/headless-agent.md) for running it as a service, updating, uninstalling, and troubleshooting. For SQLite-backed tools inside WSL, follow the [WSL SQLite setup](docs/wsl-sqlite-setup.md). ## App data App state lives in the OS user-data dir — delete it along with the app to fully uninstall. | Platform | Path | |----------|------| | macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/Token Monitor/` | | Windows | `%APPDATA%/Token Monitor/` | | Linux | `~/.config/Token Monitor/` | ## Build from source To build your own installer, use Node.js 22.15+ on the **target** OS (electron-builder can't cross-build a macOS `.dmg` on Windows, or vice-versa). ```bash npm install npm run dist:mac # macOS arm64 .dmg → dist/ npm run dist:mac:x64 # macOS Intel x64 .dmg → dist/ npm run dist:win # Windows x64 installer .exe → dist/ npm run dist:linux # Linux x64 AppImage → dist/ npm run pack # unpacked app dir (no installer), for quick local testing ``` Output lands in `dist/`. Windows and Linux use the matching `dist:*` script above on the target OS. Packaging the macOS release build requires a local Developer ID Application signing identity; use `npm start` for local development or unsupported platforms. Runtime and packaging scripts explicitly ensure the pinned tokscale binary on every target with a vendored build. Other source platforms keep the npm binary and filter clients it does not support; `npm install`, lint, and tests do not download it. For lint and tests, run `npm run verify`. Run `npm run test:coverage` for JavaScript coverage reports; see [testing and coverage](docs/testing.md) for scope, report files and interpretation limits. ## How it works ```text Mode A — Local (default, no setup) widget (Electron) ──▶ tokscale ──▶ ~/.claude, ~/.codex, $HERMES_HOME Mode B — Sync (opt-in, multi-device) device A widget ──▶ device B widget ──▶ hub ──▶ widget on any device device C agent ──▶ ``` The widget chooses local vs sync mode based on Settings → Multi-device Sync. The hub itself can run as a separate `npm run hub` process, a Cloudflare Worker, or directly inside one of the widgets (Host mode). In Hub Client and Host modes, the hub pushes aggregated stats to every connected widget over Server-Sent Events, so updates on one device usually appear on the others within a few seconds. iCloud Drive mode syncs files directly; propagation is eventually consistent and may take longer. ## Session data retention With **Preserve deleted session usage** enabled (Settings → Collection), Token Monitor archives observed daily tool/model usage locally with no time limit — so even after a source tool prunes its own sessions, the heatmap and trends are unaffected.
Advanced: extend the source tool's own retention
The heatmap and sync payload use a rolling 370-day window (older observations remain available locally for future views). **Claude Code keeps only 30 days of transcripts by default** (`cleanupPeriodDays`); to keep the full rolling year before the archive kicks in, raise it in `~/.claude/settings.json` before the window passes: ```json { "cleanupPeriodDays": 370 } ``` A larger value keeps more, at the cost of transcripts living on disk for as long as you set. tokscale's [Session Data Retention](https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale#session-data-retention) table covers the other tools' defaults and config paths. This archive only covers days Token Monitor has already observed; data deleted before it started tracking cannot be recovered.
## Settings There are two places to configure Token Monitor; day-to-day use only needs the first: - **Widget (GUI)** — click the `⚙` button in the bottom-right corner. Sections, in order: General (language, launch at login, updates), Main (Home modules and display currency), Window (window behavior, menu bar and floating-bubble layout, tray mode, shortcut), Appearance (theme and vendor colours), Collection (tracked tools, collection cadence, Preserve deleted session usage, data export), AI Tool Limits (provider selection, limits, and credentials), Subscriptions (what you pay per account), and Multi-device Sync. The `⇧` button in the title bar cycles the window behavior. - **Headless agent & hub** — no UI; configured with a `.env` file at the project root (copy from `.env.example`), precedence CLI flag → env var → built-in default. See [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md#headless-agent--hub-env). See the [configuration reference](docs/configuration.md) for every setting and all environment variables. ## Privacy Token Monitor processes usage logs locally and sends no analytics or telemetry to the project maintainer. Network access occurs only for documented or user-enabled features. See the [privacy policy](docs/privacy.md) for the data used by updates, provider integrations, Discord Rich Presence, and optional multi-device sync. ## Star History ## Contributing Issues and PRs are welcome. Start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md); project conventions, architecture notes, and the command reference live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). ## Acknowledgments - [tokscale](https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale) for log parsing and token accounting. - [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) for AI Tool Limits research. - [Code signing policy](docs/code-signing.md): Free code signing provided by [SignPath.io](https://signpath.io/), certificate by [SignPath Foundation](https://signpath.org/). ## License [MIT](LICENSE) © [@Javis](https://github.com/Javis603)

repository.readme:
# pathiel

**An AI trading agent for Hyperliquid: Claude trades perps from Claude Code, with an exact stop and target on every order.**

[![Claude Code plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude_Code-plugin-d97757.svg)](#install-in-30-seconds)
[![pathiel MCP server – quality and maintenance score on Glama](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/Julian-dev28/pathiel/badges/score.svg)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/Julian-dev28/pathiel)
[![Listed on mcpservers.org](https://mcpservers.org/badge.svg)](https://mcpservers.org/servers/julian-dev28/pathiel)
[![Version 0.7.1](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.7.1-informational.svg)](CHANGELOG.md)
[![MCP server](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-30_tools-6f42c1.svg)](docs/overhaul/MCP.md)
[![CI](https://github.com/Julian-dev28/pathiel/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/Julian-dev28/pathiel/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)


> **Real money.** A public install runs on Hyperliquid mainnet. With no key
> it only reads; once you add a key, orders are real. Read
> [Before you trade](#before-you-trade) first. Practice on testnet with one
> line: `PATHIEL_NETWORK=testnet`.

## What it does

pathiel is a free, open-source Hyperliquid MCP server and Claude Code plugin: 30 tools that read Hyperliquid perpetual futures (perps) markets and your account, and place orders, from Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor or any MCP client.
Every trade is one bracket order: an entry, a stop-loss and a take-profit target, sized from your risk profile (3x and 1% of equity per trade by default).
Desk briefs for crude oil (Brent and WTI) and metals (gold and silver) on Hyperliquid's HIP-3 markets give Claude a written call to trade from; nothing trades unless you ask.

## Install in 30 seconds

In Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add Julian-dev28/pathiel
/plugin install pathiel@pathiel
/pathiel:setup
```

From a shell instead:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add Julian-dev28/pathiel
claude plugin install pathiel@pathiel
```

Claude Code v2.1.275 or later also takes the first two lines as one:
`/plugin install pathiel --marketplace Julian-dev28/pathiel`. If Claude Code
says `Run /reload-plugins to apply`, do that, then run `/pathiel:setup`.

`/pathiel:setup` shows the network and the risks, builds a private Python
environment, creates `~/.pathiel/.env.local` (mode 600) for your keys, seeds
the default risk profile, checks the install without printing any key, and
connects the MCP server. The steps are in `commands/setup.md`.

You need Claude Code, Python 3.11 or later, and for trading a Hyperliquid
account and a browser wallet (or an API wallet you make in the Hyperliquid
app). Reading markets needs no account.
[docs/GETTING_STARTED.md](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md) walks through the
account setup.

<!-- bundle:omit -->
### Other MCP clients

Cursor, Claude Desktop, Pathiel Agent and any other MCP client register the
launcher `scripts/pathiel-mcp` from a clone as the server command, or run the
published container (amd64 and arm64). It is listed in the official MCP
registry as `io.github.Julian-dev28/pathiel`.

```bash
docker run -i --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$HOME/.pathiel:/data" \
  ghcr.io/julian-dev28/pathiel-mcp:0.7.1
```

To build it yourself: `docker build -f Dockerfile.mcp -t pathiel-mcp .`

Both are the public install: keys and config come from `~/.pathiel`, with
the same default network, profile and fee rules as the plugin. Starting
`scripts/pathiel-mcp-server.py` directly, or accepting the repo `.mcp.json`
when you open a clone in Claude Code, is the maintainer path (see
[Maintainer setup](#maintainer-setup)).
<!-- /bundle:omit -->

## First prompts to try

Paste these into Claude Code once `/mcp` shows `pathiel` connected.

| you type | what answers |
|---|---|
| What's the oil desk's call right now? | `get_desk_brief`: direction, entry, stop, target, the R it pays, and "Your size" |
| Show me BTC's order book and funding. | `get_order_book`, `get_market` |
| What's my balance and what's open? | `get_account`, `get_positions` |
| What are my risk limits? | `get_risk_limits` |
| Size a long on gold with the stop under today's low. | `size_trade` |
| Dry-run that as a bracket. | `place_bracket` with `dry_run: true`: judged and sized, nothing sent |
| Place it. | `place_bracket`: **live money**, Claude Code asks you first |
| Run one oil desk tick. | `/pathiel:desk-tick oil`: brief, sweep, levels, one decision |

## What Claude can do

`scripts/pathiel-mcp-server.py` lists 30 tools over stdio to a plugin
install: one tool per job, verb_noun names (`contracts/mcp_public`). The
maintainer's own checkout lists the 60 only, the operator set the live desks
use. Every older tool name still answers when called; it is just no longer
listed. The full table, generated from the server's own tool lists, is
[docs/overhaul/MCP.md](docs/overhaul/MCP.md).

| group | tools | names |
|---|---|---|
| Market data (no key) | 5 | `get_market`, `list_markets`, `get_candles`, `get_order_book`, `get_funding_regime` |
| Account reads | 4 | `get_account`, `get_positions`, `get_orders`, `get_history` |
| Risk and sizing | 2 | `get_risk_limits`, `size_trade` |
| Orders (live money) | 7 | `place_bracket`, `set_stop` (tighter only), `set_target`, `cancel_order`, `close_position`, `set_leverage`, `sweep_brackets` |
| Desks | 5 | `list_desks`, `get_desk_brief`, `refresh_desk`, `submit_desk_call`, `get_desk_record` |
| Setup | 4 | `get_status`, `get_config`, `update_config`, `connect_wallet` (approve an API wallet with one signature) |
| Research pool | 3 | `get_pool_status`, `join_pool`, `leave_pool` |

`get_account`, `get_positions`, `get_orders` and `get_history` take an
`address` to read any other wallet, and only read it. The server signs with
one key, yours, so it has no path to place, close or resize an order on any
other account.

The oil desk is the one active desk on a fresh install. It trades Brent
(`xyz:BRENTOIL`) on mainnet, and WTI (`xyz:CL`) on testnet, where Brent is
not listed. The metals desk (gold, silver) is registered and off by default;
`get_desk_brief` still reads it. The rules each bracket must pass are in
[docs/strategy/OIL_RULES.md](docs/strategy/OIL_RULES.md).

## Before you trade

### Networks and modes

The mode follows from what is in `~/.pathiel/.env.local`:

| you have | mode | what works |
|---|---|---|
| no key | read-only, mainnet (the default) data | every read tool; order tools answer that no key is configured |
| an [API wallet](https://app.hyperliquid.xyz/API) key | mainnet (the default) | everything, with real money |
| a key and `PATHIEL_NETWORK=testnet` | testnet | everything, with test funds; the oil desk trades WTI (`xyz:CL`) |

**Connect your wallet** is the quick way to a key: `/pathiel:setup` (or
asking Claude to connect your wallet) runs `connect_wallet`. It makes a new
API wallet key on your machine and opens a local page where your browser
wallet approves it with one signature, on the network you run. The key goes
into `~/.pathiel/.env.local` (mode 600) and nowhere else: it can trade, never
withdraw, and your main key never leaves the wallet. Pasting an API wallet
from the Hyperliquid app by hand still works.

State (theses, journals, caches) is kept per network, so testnet and mainnet
never share it. Testnet needs its own API wallet, created and approved in the
[testnet app](https://app.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz/API). How to create one,
step by step: [Connect your Hyperliquid account](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md#connect-your-hyperliquid-account).
The network is read once when the server starts: after editing the env file,
reconnect pathiel in `/mcp`.

### How the safety works

- **An exact stop on every order.** `place_bracket` is the one entry path:
  entry, stop and target together. It refuses a bracket that pays under 2R,
  and a stop that sits outside half the distance to liquidation. A market
  entry fills first and its stop goes on right after; if the venue refuses
  that stop, the output says `FILLED WITHOUT A STOP` and `sweep_brackets`
  checks every open position for one.
- **Default profile: 3x, 1%, one position.** At most 3x leverage, 1% of
  equity at the stop per trade (up to 2% only when the venue's minimum order
  size forces it), one position at a time. `set_leverage` refuses above the
  cap. You change the profile with `update_config` or in
  `~/.pathiel/.agent-config.json`; nothing raises it for you.
- **Read-only without a key.** No key, no orders. The API wallet key can
  trade and can never withdraw.
- **Testnet when you want it.** `PATHIEL_NETWORK=testnet` in
  `~/.pathiel/.env.local` switches to test funds.
- **Claude Code asks before each live-money call.** The seven order tools,
  and `update_config`, are marked destructive, so Claude Code asks you before each
  call unless you allow the tool for good. Nothing runs in the background:
  no bot, no scheduler. The `/loop` desk tick trades only while your session runs it.

### Builder fee

None. pathiel is free: no order it places carries a Hyperliquid builder fee,
so you pay only Hyperliquid's own trading fee. There is nothing to approve.

### If a fee ever comes back

It would ship as a new version with the rate in the changelog, and it could
not touch your orders on its own: Hyperliquid charges a builder fee only
after you approve that exact rate with your master wallet, and rejects any
order whose builder fee is above the max you approved. Hyperliquid caps a
perp builder fee at 0.1%. If you approved the 0.01% fee of pathiel 0.4.0,
it is no longer charged; [docs/BUILDER_FEE.md](docs/BUILDER_FEE.md) shows
how to revoke it anyway.

### Risk

Leveraged perps can lose the whole account, fast. The default profile limits
how much one trade can lose at its stop; it does not limit gaps, slippage or
a run of losses. The profile's daily loss figure is shown, not enforced.
There is no demonstrated edge and no return is promised. This is software,
not financial advice. You decide every trade and carry its result.

### Restricted jurisdictions

Hyperliquid's terms bar use from restricted jurisdictions, including by US
persons. The current list is in Hyperliquid's terms. pathiel does not check
where you are; staying within the rules where you live is on you.

### Your data

pathiel runs on your computer and the project runs no server, so nothing is
sent to the maintainer. No analytics, no telemetry. What does leave your
machine:

- **Hyperliquid API** (api.hyperliquid.xyz, or the testnet API): market and
  account reads, the orders you ask for, the API wallet approval you sign.
- **Public data feeds** the desk briefs read: EIA, FRED, CFTC, Congress and
  the Federal Register, prediction markets and news. An optional API key
  for one of them goes only to that feed.
- **GitHub**, only if you join the research pool: the signed statement you
  submit as a pull request.

Keys, theses, the desk journal and your config stay in `~/.pathiel`.
Details: [docs/PRIVACY.md](docs/PRIVACY.md).

## Research pool (opt-in)

pathiel can grade your trades alongside everyone else's. You register your
Hyperliquid address with one signed statement; you upload nothing, since
pathiel only reads fills Hyperliquid already makes public. From the time
you join, your public fills on the pool coins (`xyz:BRENTOIL`, `xyz:CL`,
`xyz:SILVER`, `xyz:GOLD`) are graded with the same harness the project runs
on its own trades, and published on a public scoreboard at least 24 hours
late.

What you get: your own graded report (fluke or edge on your trades, with
ranges, through `get_pool_status` with `report: true`), and pool-level stats on which desks and
setups hold up across members.

What it is not: not a fee waiver, since pathiel charges no fee to anyone,
member or not, and joining never changes what you pay. No payout, refund or reward is ever
tied to your returns. Not a copy-trading feed: results are published at
least 24 hours late, never live. No edge is demonstrated by joining, or by
anything the pool's stats show.

Run `/pathiel:share` to join or leave. It shows you the exact statement
before it signs anything, and the pull request it opens for you.

Scoreboard: https://julian-dev28.github.io/pathiel/scoreboard/

### Privacy

What is public: your account address (shortened, with an explorer link),
the date you joined, your closed and graded trade counts, your graded row
(win rate, mean result in R, a label, a luck score), and pool totals that
include your trades. What is never public: anything closed in the last 24
hours, any open position, single trades, prices, sizes, dollar results,
account value, leverage, or any key.

Leaving is one more signed statement, or a request in a GitHub issue with
no signature. Coming back takes a new signed join; only trades after the
new join count, and deleting a leave file never brings an account back on
its own.

Full details, including the exact text you sign: [docs/PRIVACY.md](docs/PRIVACY.md).

## FAQ

**How do I connect Claude to Hyperliquid?**
Install pathiel as a Claude Code plugin with the three lines in
[Install in 30 seconds](#install-in-30-seconds). Market data works at once
with no key; add an API wallet key to `~/.pathiel/.env.local` to trade.
Claude Desktop, Cursor and other MCP clients use the launcher or the
container described in [Other MCP clients](#other-mcp-clients). No
Anthropic API key is needed: the one model step, the desk thesis behind
`refresh_desk`, runs through your local Claude Code CLI.

**Is pathiel a Hyperliquid trading bot?**
No, and it never trades on its own. It is an MCP server that gives Claude
tools: Claude places an order when you ask for one in the session, and
Claude Code asks before each live-money call. `/loop 15m /pathiel:desk-tick oil`
re-prompts Claude on a timer, only while that session stays open.

**Can it withdraw my money?**
No. pathiel signs with an API wallet, which Hyperliquid lets trade and never
withdraw. Your master key is never stored, and pathiel needs it for nothing:
the only script that takes it revokes a builder fee approval, at a hidden
prompt in your own terminal.

**Does pathiel charge a fee?**
No. Orders carry no builder fee; you pay Hyperliquid's own trading fee
only.

**How do I practice without real money?**
Add `PATHIEL_NETWORK=testnet` to `~/.pathiel/.env.local`, create an API
wallet in the testnet app (app.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz), and reconnect
pathiel in `/mcp`. The oil desk trades WTI (`xyz:CL`) there.

**Is there an edge?**
None is demonstrated. The desk briefs are a structured, written call with
levels, not a forecast. `get_desk_record` grades every call in the open.

**How do I remove it?**
Revoke the API wallet in the Hyperliquid app (More, API), then
`claude plugin uninstall pathiel@pathiel` and delete `~/.pathiel` if you want
the keys and state gone.

## Maintainer setup

> Maintainer path: this runs mainnet with the tracked repo config (20x, whole-equity sizing). It is not the public install.

This is how the maintainer runs pathiel on his own account, from a checkout.
It is not the public install and its numbers are not the defaults.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Julian-dev28/pathiel
cd pathiel
cp .env.local.example .env.local
scripts/restart.sh          # FastAPI Desk page on http://localhost:8000/ and the log rotator
scripts/restart.sh status
```

- **MCP server.** The repo `.mcp.json` starts
  `scripts/pathiel-mcp-server.py` directly, with no install marker, so it
  runs mainnet on the tracked `.agent-config.json`. Opening a clone in
  Claude Code offers that server; accepting it is the maintainer path, not
  the public install. Other clients that want the public path register
  `scripts/pathiel-mcp`.
- **Risk profile.** The tracked config sets 20x, the whole equity per
  position less the opening fee, one position. The rules `place_bracket`
  enforces (2R minimum, stop inside half the distance to liquidation, one
  slot) hold on both paths.
- **Desk loop.** `.claude/skills/desk-tick/SKILL.md` on `/loop 15m /desk-tick oil`.
  `scripts/build_plugin_skill.py` generates the plugin copies under
  `skills/` and `agents/`; the gate fails when a copy is stale.
- **Gate.** `PATHIEL_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`,
  offline, run by `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` (`scripts/install_hooks.sh`
  wires it in). `scripts/mcp_tool_table.py` regenerates the tool table;
  `.venv/bin/python scripts/mcp_smoke.py` is a live, read-only MCP smoke.
- **Keys.** `scripts/preflight_secrets.py` checks the env file without
  printing it; `docs/SECRETS.md` lists every secret and how to rotate it.

name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

# The job reads the repo and nothing else. Without this block GITHUB_TOKEN gets
# the repository's default, which can be read/write on every scope: a step
# compromised through a dependency could then push, tag or open releases.
permissions:
  contents: read

# Actions are pinned to a full commit SHA, not a tag. A tag is a pointer the
# action's owner (or whoever holds their token) can move; tj-actions/changed-
# files (March 2025, CVE-2025-30066) moved every tag to a payload that printed
# runner secrets. The comment names the release the SHA was taken from;
# tests/test_supply_chain.py fails on any `uses:` that is not a 40-hex SHA.

jobs:
  test:
    name: Tests (Python ${{ matrix.python-version }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # 3.13 is what the desk runs on (the operator's .venv, 2026-10-25);
        # 3.11 is the floor pyproject declares. A green matrix that skips the
        # production interpreter is not evidence about production.
        python-version: ["3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1

      - name: Set up Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0  # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: requirements.lock

      # Install the EXACT pinned set, not a fresh resolve of the ranges in
      # pyproject.toml. A green CI against a different dependency set than
      # production runs is not evidence about production.
      - name: Install (pinned)
        run: |
          pip install -r requirements.lock
          pip install -e . --no-deps

      # This repo was green locally and red on CI for weeks because 50 files
      # hardcoded /Users/julian_dev/... Cheap check, runs before the suite so
      # the failure names the actual cause instead of a FileNotFoundError.
      - name: No machine-bound absolute paths
        run: python scripts/check_no_absolute_paths.py

      # pytest's addopts deselects the `online` and `live` markers, so this runs
      # only the offline suite — no network, no real-money orders, CI-safe.
      # -rs prints the reason for every skip. Without it the summary says
      # "18 skipped" and nothing else, so a guard that quietly stopped running
      # in this environment looks exactly like a green build.
      - name: Run offline test suite
        run: pytest -rs
sampled_files.Dockerfile:
# Base image pinned by digest (the multi-arch index for python:3.11-slim,
# Debian 13, resolved 2026-10-25). A tag is a pointer Docker Hub can move; the
# digest is the bytes. Bump it on purpose:
#   docker buildx imagetools inspect python:3.11-slim | grep Digest
FROM python:3.11-slim@sha256:07d4824036af339fa1b6ef769cc99d9c10a141769538b52b3b597c84f7a7b535 AS base

ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1 \
    PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1

# The app runs as this user, never as root (security review 2026-10-25).
# docker-entrypoint.sh starts as root only where it has to (a Fly volume is
# mounted root-owned), hands /data to this user, and drops to it with setpriv
# before exec. k8s sets runAsUser to the same uid, so there not even the
# entrypoint has root.
RUN groupadd --system --gid 10001 pathiel \
 && useradd --system --uid 10001 --gid pathiel --home-dir /app --shell /usr/sbin/nologin pathiel

WORKDIR /app

# Install deps first so `pip install` is cached across code changes.
#
# From requirements.lock, hash-checked, then the package itself with
# --no-deps. Until 2026-10-25 this was a bare `pip install -e .`, which
# resolved the RANGES in pyproject.toml fresh on every build: the image ran
# whatever PyPI served that day, not the set CI tested, and nothing checked a
# single file's hash. (requests and websocket-client still arrive as
# transitive deps of hyperliquid-python-sdk; the lock lists them.) The lock
# also carries the dev extras (pytest, ruff); they cost a few MB and keep one
# lock for CI and prod. No compiler needed: every pin ships a manylinux wheel.
COPY requirements.lock ./
RUN pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.lock
COPY pyproject.toml ./
COPY pathiel/__init__.py pathiel/__init__.py
RUN pip install --no-deps -e .

# Copy every top-level source package a managed process actually imports at
# runtime. `scripts/restart.sh` is the source of truth for what runs:
#   pathiel/              core package — server, dashboard, agents, client
#                                (imported by every process below)
#   scripts/                    the MCP server, log_rotate.py, the desk-tick
#                                tools (desk_slot.py, oil_levels.py), CLI tooling
#   services/intel/             desk news/policy/catalyst/odds/positioning
#                                packet (services.intel.api.build_packet —
#                                imported by services/strategies)
# `services/pathiel_data_api` is its OWN deploy unit — own Dockerfile, own
# Postgres, own requirements.txt (sqlalchemy/psycopg2, never installed here)
# — deliberately NOT bundled into this image. `docs/`, `tests/`, and
# `skills/` are excluded via .dockerignore; see that file for the full list
# and why. (`services/trend_engine` and `research/` were deleted 2026-10-25.)
COPY pathiel/ pathiel/
# The shared pydantic contracts every service imports at module load
# (pathiel.agents.config_store -> contracts.risk.models on the server's
# first import). Missing until 2026-10-25: the image built fine and
# `python -m pathiel.server` died with ModuleNotFoundError.
COPY contracts/ contracts/
COPY scripts/ scripts/
# Auth is on the request path for every gated route, so a missing copy here is
# not a degraded feature, it is a server that 500s on the first page load.
COPY services/auth/ services/auth/
# server.py mounts this router unconditionally (/api/desks, /desks/...) —
# same "500 on first import" reasoning as auth above.
COPY services/strategies/ services/strategies/
# Zero-LLM news/policy/catalyst/odds/positioning packet services/strategies
# imports (services.intel.api.build_packet) — same reasoning again.
COPY services/intel/ services/intel/
# LLM gateway (local Claude Code CLI only) and the desk thesis writer on top
# of it. The image has no claude CLI, so in a container write_thesis degrades
# to the previous thesis or a flat placeholder instead of crashing.
COPY services/llm/ services/llm/
COPY services/thesis/ services/thesis/
# Account registry, vault and credentials (the connect flow). server.py mounts
# services.accounts.api, so it must ship: same reasoning as auth above.
COPY services/accounts/ services/accounts/
# server.py mounts services.risk.api (risk_limits/risk_size_trade and the
# place_bracket feasibility check both derive through it).
COPY services/risk/ services/risk/
# The trade review (python3 -m services.review run): read-only ledger, stats
# and backtest proposals. Not on the request path; shipped so the image can
# run the daily review against its own state volume.
COPY services/review/ services/review/
# The research pool's CODE only (python3 -m services.pool). Not on the request
# path, and this image cannot run the scoreboard build: it does not hold pool/
# (the signed member files) or docs/scoreboard/ (the output, a tracked file
# the maintainer commits). The build runs from the maintainer's checkout. The
# line is here because tests/test_deploy_config.py wants a COPY for every
# services package that code under pathiel/, scripts/ or services/ imports.
COPY services/pool/ services/pool/
COPY conftest.py ./

# ── Runtime state ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# State lives on a persistent volume mounted at /data (k8s
# volumeClaimTemplates, or `docker run -v`) so `web` keeps one source of truth
# across restarts and redeploys.
#
# Almost every state path in this app routes through PATHIEL_STATE_DIR (see
# pathiel/state.py:state_file — backup receipts and other process-local
# state files all resolve relative to it; also services/*/env.py).
# Pointing that ONE var at /data/.state redirects all of them together.
# docker-entrypoint.sh creates the real /data/.state directory at container
# start (the volume is empty/fresh at that point, not at image-build time).
#
# 2026-10-23 (wave 2): PATHIEL_DSL_STATE_FILE and PATHIEL_AGENT_MEMORY_FILE
# are dropped — pathiel.agents.dsl_exit and pathiel.agents.memory, their only
# readers, are retired with the rest of the autonomous engine. The
# scripts/scheduler.py symlink workaround this section used to carry is
# dropped the same wave: scheduler.py itself is deleted. 2026-10-25:
# PATHIEL_POSITIONS_SNAPSHOT_FILE goes too — the loop that wrote the snapshot
# is gone, so the dashboard reads positions live (cached) and the module
# that read the file is deleted.

# HOME on the volume: pathiel/client/universe.py caches under ~/.pathiel and
# scripts/backup_state.py defaults to ~/pathiel-backups. As root HOME was
# /root; the app user may not write there, and on k8s the root filesystem is
# read-only, so the one writable, persistent place is /data.
ENV HOME=/data/home

ENV SESSION_LOG_PATH=/data/session-log.jsonl \
    PATHIEL_AGENT_CONFIG_FILE=/data/.agent-config.json \
    PATHIEL_STATE_DIR=/data/.state

# ── Networking ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# pathiel/server.py defaults PATHIEL_BIND to 127.0.0.1 (a 2026-07-10
# security fix for running bare on an operator's Mac, so the dashboard isn't
# reachable from the LAN by default). Inside a container that default makes
# the process unreachable from anywhere OUTSIDE its own network namespace —
# `docker run -p` and k8s probes/Services all connect from outside it, so the
# request never lands and every health check times out. 0.0.0.0 is correct
# and safe here: the container/pod boundary is the actual security perimeter
# (the k8s Service, or whatever fronts `docker run`), not the loopback
# interface.
ENV PATHIEL_BIND=0.0.0.0

# No LLM credential is baked in or expected. The one LLM step (the desk thesis
# writer, services/thesis via services/llm) shells out to a LOCALLY
# AUTHENTICATED Claude Code CLI session: an operator's desktop subscription,
# not a credential that can be passed as a secret. In a container
# desk_refresh degrades to the previous thesis or a flat placeholder; the
# operator refreshes theses from their own machine through the MCP server.
# (The AI_BRAIN_PROVIDER / OPENROUTER_API_KEY pair this section used to set
# left with pathiel/agents/ai_brain.py on 2026-10-25.)

# Every managed process shares this one bootstrap step (see the script for
# why) before running its real command.
COPY docker-entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh
RUN chmod 0755 /usr/local/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh \
 && mkdir -p /app/logs /data/.state /data/home \
 && chown -R pathiel:pathiel /app/logs /data
# Source stays root-owned and read-only to the app user: code that is
# compromised at runtime cannot rewrite itself for the next restart. Only
# /app/logs (log_rotate.py) and /data (state) are the app's to write.
ENTRYPOINT ["docker-entrypoint.sh"]

EXPOSE 8000

# Default command runs the FastAPI server (dashboard + API). The log rotator
# runs as a second k8s container sharing this same image — see
# k8s/statefulset.yaml. (There is no trading loop or scheduler process since
# 2026-10-23; Claude is the trader, via the MCP server on the operator's
# machine. Fly.io was dropped as a target 2026-10-25.)
CMD ["python3", "-m", "pathiel.server"]

sampled_files.README.md:
# pathiel

**An AI trading agent for Hyperliquid: Claude trades perps from Claude Code, with an exact stop and target on every order.**

[![Claude Code plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude_Code-plugin-d97757.svg)](#install-in-30-seconds)
[![pathiel MCP server – quality and maintenance score on Glama](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/Julian-dev28/pathiel/badges/score.svg)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/Julian-dev28/pathiel)
[![Listed on mcpservers.org](https://mcpservers.org/badge.svg)](https://mcpservers.org/servers/julian-dev28/pathiel)
[![Version 0.7.1](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.7.1-informational.svg)](CHANGELOG.md)
[![MCP server](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-30_tools-6f42c1.svg)](docs/overhaul/MCP.md)
[![CI](https://github.com/Julian-dev28/pathiel/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/Julian-dev28/pathiel/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)


> **Real money.** A public install runs on Hyperliquid mainnet. With no key
> it only reads; once you add a key, orders are real. Read
> [Before you trade](#before-you-trade) first. Practice on testnet with one
> line: `PATHIEL_NETWORK=testnet`.

## What it does

pathiel is a free, open-source Hyperliquid MCP server and Claude Code plugin: 30 tools that read Hyperliquid perpetual futures (perps) markets and your account, and place orders, from Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor or any MCP client.
Every trade is one bracket order: an entry, a stop-loss and a take-profit target, sized from your risk profile (3x and 1% of equity per trade by default).
Desk briefs for crude oil (Brent and WTI) and metals (gold and silver) on Hyperliquid's HIP-3 markets give Claude a written call to trade from; nothing trades unless you ask.

## Install in 30 seconds

In Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add Julian-dev28/pathiel
/plugin install pathiel@pathiel
/pathiel:setup
```

From a shell instead:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add Julian-dev28/pathiel
claude plugin install pathiel@pathiel
```

Claude Code v2.1.275 or later also takes the first two lines as one:
`/plugin install pathiel --marketplace Julian-dev28/pathiel`. If Claude Code
says `Run /reload-plugins to apply`, do that, then run `/pathiel:setup`.

`/pathiel:setup` shows the network and the risks, builds a private Python
environment, creates `~/.pathiel/.env.local` (mode 600) for your keys, seeds
the default risk profile, checks the install without printing any key, and
connects the MCP server. The steps are in `commands/setup.md`.

You need Claude Code, Python 3.11 or later, and for trading a Hyperliquid
account and a browser wallet (or an API wallet you make in the Hyperliquid
app). Reading markets needs no account.
[docs/GETTING_STARTED.md](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md) walks through the
account setup.

<!-- bundle:omit -->
### Other MCP clients

Cursor, Claude Desktop, Pathiel Agent and any other MCP client register the
launcher `scripts/pathiel-mcp` from a clone as the server command, or run the
published container (amd64 and arm64). It is listed in the official MCP
registry as `io.github.Julian-dev28/pathiel`.

```bash
docker run -i --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$HOME/.pathiel:/data" \
  ghcr.io/julian-dev28/pathiel-mcp:0.7.1
```

To build it yourself: `docker build -f Dockerfile.mcp -t pathiel-mcp .`

Both are the public install: keys and config come from `~/.pathiel`, with
the same default network, profile and fee rules as the plugin. Starting
`scripts/pathiel-mcp-server.py` directly, or accepting the repo `.mcp.json`
when you open a clone in Claude Code, is the maintainer path (see
[Maintainer setup](#maintainer-setup)).
<!-- /bundle:omit -->

## First prompts to try

Paste these into Claude Code once `/mcp` shows `pathiel` connected.

| you type | what answers |
|---|---|
| What's the oil desk's call right now? | `get_desk_brief`: direction, entry, stop, target, the R it pays, and "Your size" |
| Show me BTC's order book and funding. | `get_order_book`, `get_market` |
| What's my balance and what's open? | `get_account`, `get_positions` |
| What are my risk limits? | `get_risk_limits` |
| Size a long on gold with the stop under today's low. | `size_trade` |
| Dry-run that as a bracket. | `place_bracket` with `dry_run: true`: judged and sized, nothing sent |
| Place it. | `place_bracket`: **live money**, Claude Code asks you first |
| Run one oil desk tick. | `/pathiel:desk-tick oil`: brief, sweep, levels, one decision |

## What Claude can do

`scripts/pathiel-mcp-server.py` lists 30 tools over stdio to a plugin
install: one tool per job, verb_noun names (`contracts/mcp_public`). The
maintainer's own checkout lists the 60 only, the operator set the live desks
use. Every older tool name still answers when called; it is just no longer
listed. The full table, generated from the server's own tool lists, is
[docs/overhaul/MCP.md](docs/overhaul/MCP.md).

| group | tools | names |
|---|---|---|
| Market data (no key) | 5 | `get_market`, `list_markets`, `get_candles`, `get_order_book`, `get_funding_regime` |
| Account reads | 4 | `get_account`, `get_positions`, `get_orders`, `get_history` |
| Risk and sizing | 2 | `get_risk_limits`, `size_trade` |
| Orders (live money) | 7 | `place_bracket`, `set_stop` (tighter only), `set_target`, `cancel_order`, `close_position`, `set_leverage`, `sweep_brackets` |
| Desks | 5 | `list_desks`, `get_desk_brief`, `refresh_desk`, `submit_desk_call`, `get_desk_record` |
| Setup | 4 | `get_status`, `get_config`, `update_config`, `connect_wallet` (approve an API wallet with one signature) |
| Research pool | 3 | `get_pool_status`, `join_pool`, `leave_pool` |

`get_account`, `get_positions`, `get_orders` and `get_history` take an
`address` to read any other wallet, and only read it. The server signs with
one key, yours, so it has no path to place, close or resize an order on any
other account.

The oil desk is the one active desk on a fresh install. It trades Brent
(`xyz:BRENTOIL`) on mainnet, and WTI (`xyz:CL`) on testnet, where Brent is
not listed. The metals desk (gold, silver) is registered and off by default;
`get_desk_brief` still reads it. The rules each bracket must pass are in
[docs/strategy/OIL_RULES.md](docs/strategy/OIL_RULES.md).

## Before you trade

### Networks and modes

The mode follows from what is in `~/.pathiel/.env.local`:

| you have | mode | what works |
|---|---|---|
| no key | read-only, mainnet (the default) data | every read tool; order tools answer that no key is configured |
| an [API wallet](https://app.hyperliquid.xyz/API) key | mainnet (the default) | everything, with real money |
| a key and `PATHIEL_NETWORK=testnet` | testnet | everything, with test funds; the oil desk trades WTI (`xyz:CL`) |

**Connect your wallet** is the quick way to a key: `/pathiel:setup` (or
asking Claude to connect your wallet) runs `connect_wallet`. It makes a new
API wallet key on your machine and opens a local page where your browser
wallet approves it with one signature, on the network you run. The key goes
into `~/.pathiel/.env.local` (mode 600) and nowhere else: it can trade, never
withdraw, and your main key never leaves the wallet. Pasting an API wallet
from the Hyperliquid app by hand still works.

State (theses, journals, caches) is kept per network, so testnet and mainnet
never share it. Testnet needs its own API wallet, created and approved in the
[testnet app](https://app.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz/API). How to create one,
step by step: [Connect your Hyperliquid account](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md#connect-your-hyperliquid-account).
The network is read once when the server starts: after editing the env file,
reconnect pathiel in `/mcp`.

### How the safety works

- **An exact stop on every order.** `place_bracket` is the one entry path:
  entry, stop and target together. It refuses a bracket that pays under 2R,
  and a stop that sits outside half the distance to liquidation. A market
  entry fills first and its stop goes on right after; if the venue refuses
  that stop, the output says `FILLED WITHOUT A STOP` and `sweep_brackets`
  checks every open position for one.
- **Default profile: 3x, 1%, one position.** At most 3x leverage, 1% of
  equity at the stop per trade (up to 2% only when the venue's minimum order
  size forces it), one position at a time. `set_leverage` refuses above the
  cap. You change the profile with `update_config` or in
  `~/.pathiel/.agent-config.json`; nothing raises it for you.
- **Read-only without a key.** No key, no orders. The API wallet key can
  trade and can never withdraw.
- **Testnet when you want it.** `PATHIEL_NETWORK=testnet` in
  `~/.pathiel/.env.local` switches to test funds.
- **Claude Code asks before each live-money call.** The seven order tools,
  and `update_config`, are marked destructive, so Claude Code asks you before each
  call unless you allow the tool for good. Nothing runs in the background:
  no bot, no scheduler. The `/loop` desk tick trades only while your session runs it.

### Builder fee

None. pathiel is free: no order it places carries a Hyperliquid builder fee,
so you pay only Hyperliquid's own trading fee. There is nothing to approve.

### If a fee ever comes back

It would ship as a new version with the rate in the changelog, and it could
not touch your orders on its own: Hyperliquid charges a builder fee only
after you approve that exact rate with your master wallet, and rejects any
order whose builder fee is above the max you approved. Hyperliquid caps a
perp builder fee at 0.1%. If you approved the 0.01% fee of pathiel 0.4.0,
it is no longer charged; [docs/BUILDER_FEE.md](docs/BUILDER_FEE.md) shows
how to revoke it anyway.

### Risk

Leveraged perps can lose the whole account, fast. The default profile limits
how much one trade can lose at its stop; it does not limit gaps, slippage or
a run of losses. The profile's daily loss figure is shown, not enforced.
There is no demonstrated edge and no return is promised. This is software,
not financial advice. You decide every trade and carry its result.

### Restricted jurisdictions

Hyperliquid's terms bar use from restricted jurisdictions, including by US
persons. The current list is in Hyperliquid's terms. pathiel does not check
where you are; staying within the rules where you live is on you.

### Your data

pathiel runs on your computer and the project runs no server, so nothing is
sent to the maintainer. No analytics, no telemetry. What does leave your
machine:

- **Hyperliquid API** (api.hyperliquid.xyz, or the testnet API): market and
  account reads, the orders you ask for, the API wallet approval you sign.
- **Public data feeds** the desk briefs read: EIA, FRED, CFTC, Congress and
  the Federal Register, prediction markets and news. An optional API key
  for one of them goes only to that feed.
- **GitHub**, only if you join the research pool: the signed statement you
  submit as a pull request.

Keys, theses, the desk journal and your config stay in `~/.pathiel`.
Details: [docs/PRIVACY.md](docs/PRIVACY.md).

## Research pool (opt-in)

pathiel can grade your trades alongside everyone else's. You register your
Hyperliquid address with one signed statement; you upload nothing, since
pathiel only reads fills Hyperliquid already makes public. From the time
you join, your public fills on the pool coins (`xyz:BRENTOIL`, `xyz:CL`,
`xyz:SILVER`, `xyz:GOLD`) are graded with the same harness the project runs
on its own trades, and published on a public scoreboard at least 24 hours
late.

What you get: your own graded report (fluke or edge on your trades, with
ranges, through `get_pool_status` with `report: true`), and pool-level stats on which desks and
setups hold up across members.

What it is not: not a fee waiver, since pathiel charges no fee to anyone,
member or not, and joining never changes what you pay. No payout, refund or reward is ever
tied to your returns. Not a copy-trading feed: results are published at
least 24 hours late, never live. No edge is demonstrated by joining, or by
anything the pool's stats show.

Run `/pathiel:share` to join or leave. It shows you the exact statement
before it signs anything, and the pull request it opens for you.

Scoreboard: https://julian-dev28.github.io/pathiel/scoreboard/

### Privacy

What is public: your account address (shortened, with an explorer link),
the date you joined, your closed and graded trade counts, your graded row
(win rate, mean result in R, a label, a luck score), and pool totals that
include your trades. What is never public: anything closed in the last 24
hours, any open position, single trades, prices, sizes, dollar results,
account value, leverage, or any key.

Leaving is one more signed statement, or a request in a GitHub issue with
no signature. Coming back takes a new signed join; only trades after the
new join count, and deleting a leave file never brings an account back on
its own.

Full details, including the exact text you sign: [docs/PRIVACY.md](docs/PRIVACY.md).

## FAQ

**How do I connect Claude to Hyperliquid?**
Install pathiel as a Claude Code plugin with the three lines in
[Install in 30 seconds](#install-in-30-seconds). Market data works at once
with no key; add an API wallet key to `~/.pathiel/.env.local` to trade.
Claude Desktop, Cursor and other MCP clients use the launcher or the
container described in [Other MCP clients](#other-mcp-clients). No
Anthropic API key is needed: the one model step, the desk thesis behind
`refresh_desk`, runs through your local Claude Code CLI.

**Is pathiel a Hyperliquid trading bot?**
No, and it never trades on its own. It is an MCP server that gives Claude
tools: Claude places an order when you ask for one in the session, and
Claude Code asks before each live-money call. `/loop 15m /pathiel:desk-tick oil`
re-prompts Claude on a timer, only while that session stays open.

**Can it withdraw my money?**
No. pathiel signs with an API wallet, which Hyperliquid lets trade and never
withdraw. Your master key is never stored, and pathiel needs it for nothing:
the only script that takes it revokes a builder fee approval, at a hidden
prompt in your own terminal.

**Does pathiel charge a fee?**
No. Orders carry no builder fee; you pay Hyperliquid's own trading fee
only.

**How do I practice without real money?**
Add `PATHIEL_NETWORK=testnet` to `~/.pathiel/.env.local`, create an API
wallet in the testnet app (app.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz), and reconnect
pathiel in `/mcp`. The oil desk trades WTI (`xyz:CL`) there.

**Is there an edge?**
None is demonstrated. The desk briefs are a structured, written call with
levels, not a forecast. `get_desk_record` grades every call in the open.

**How do I remove it?**
Revoke the API wallet in the Hyperliquid app (More, API), then
`claude plugin uninstall pathiel@pathiel` and delete `~/.pathiel` if you want
the keys and state gone.

## Maintainer setup

> Maintainer path: this runs mainnet with the tracked repo config (20x, whole-equity sizing). It is not the public install.

This is how the maintainer runs pathiel on his own account, from a checkout.
It is not the public install and its numbers are not the defaults.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Julian-dev28/pathiel
cd pathiel
cp .env.local.example .env.local
scripts/restart.sh          # FastAPI Desk page on http://localhost:8000/ and the log rotator
scripts/restart.sh status
```

- **MCP server.** The repo `.mcp.json` starts
  `scripts/pathiel-mcp-server.py` directly, with no install marker, so it
  runs mainnet on the tracked `.agent-config.json`. Opening a clone in
  Claude Code offers that server; accepting it is the maintainer path, not
  the public install. Other clients that want the public path register
  `scripts/pathiel-mcp`.
- **Risk profile.** The tracked config sets 20x, the whole equity per
  position less the opening fee, one position. The rules `place_bracket`
  enforces (2R minimum, stop inside half the distance to liquidation, one
  slot) hold on both paths.
- **Desk loop.** `.claude/skills/desk-tick/SKILL.md` on `/loop 15m /desk-tick oil`.
  `scripts/build_plugin_skill.py` generates the plugin copies under
  `skills/` and `agents/`; the gate fails when a copy is stale.
- **Gate.** `PATHIEL_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`,
  offline, run by `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` (`scripts/install_hooks.sh`
  wires it in). `scripts/mcp_tool_table.py` regenerates the tool table;
  `.venv/bin/python scripts/mcp_smoke.py` is a live, read-only MCP smoke.
- **Keys.** `scripts/preflight_secrets.py` checks the env file without
  printing it; `docs/SECRETS.md` lists every secret and how to rotate it.

More: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the code layout,
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for the hardening checks.

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "pathiel"
dynamic = ["version"]
description = "Autonomous quant trading agent for Hyperliquid perpetual markets"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = [
    "fastapi>=0.115,<1",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.30,<1",
    "httpx>=0.27,<1",
    "pydantic>=2.0",
    "pydantic_settings>=2.0",
    "python-dotenv>=1.0",
    "hyperliquid-python-sdk>=0.23.0",
    "eth-account>=0.13.0",
    "msgpack>=1.1.0",
    "prometheus-client>=0.20",
    "finlight-client==2.4.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.0",
    "ruff>=0.4",
]

[project.scripts]
pathiel = "pathiel.__main__:main"

[tool.hatch.version]
path = "pathiel/__init__.py"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["pathiel"]

[tool.ruff]
# research/ (exploratory scratch, 175MB with caches) was deleted 2026-10-25;
# the vendored .agents/.forge/.qwen skill copies went 2026-10-17.
exclude = [".venv"]
line-length = 100

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Gate on pyflakes only, and mean it. F is the rule class that finds bugs rather
# than opinions: undefined names, unused imports, duplicate dict keys. It earned
# the slot on 2026-09-02, when a first run found `stop_ws_mids()` in the
# exchange client using a lock that is defined nowhere — an exported function
# that could only ever raise NameError — plus a test fixture whose duplicate
# "unlock_short" key silently dropped a live book's stop_pct.
#
# The E (pycodestyle) rules are deliberately NOT gated. Every one of them fires
# on a convention this codebase uses on purpose: E402 on the import-order
# comments that exist because `rebalancer_owned` freezes the state directory at
# import time, and E741 on `h, l, c` — which is OHLC, not an ambiguous name.
# A gate that cries wolf gets bypassed, and --no-verify is banned here.
select = ["F"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["."]
# services/*/tests too: a service whose suite is not collected is a service
# whose suite does not exist. services/auth is on every request path.
testpaths = ["tests", "services", "contracts"]
addopts = "-m 'not online and not live and not browser'"
markers = [
    "browser: drives a real Chromium via Playwright and boots a server; too slow for the commit gate, deselected by default (run with: pytest -m browser)",
    "online: exercises the live Hyperliquid public API (read-only); deselected by default (run with: pytest -m online)",
    "live: real-money e2e — places orders and calls the billable LLM; deselected by default and additionally requires PATHIEL_E2E=1 (run with: PATHIEL_E2E=1 pytest -m live)",
]

# ✨ pi-hypercharm-provider **17+ models through [Charm Hyper](https://hyper.charm.land/)** _Hyperoptimized coding models — DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, MiniMax, Gemma, GPT-OSS, and Llama for [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi-coding-agent)._ [![pi extension](https://img.shields.io/badge/pi-extension-blueviolet)](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi-coding-agent) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](./LICENSE)
## Pi 1.0 compatibility Tested with Pi **1.0.0**. Host-provided packages remain wildcard peers; development uses exact SDK pins. Run `bun run test:pi` for offline manifest, catalog, lifecycle and streaming checks. To test an installed host, set `PI1_HOST_PACKAGE` to its package directory; add `PI1_HOST_ENTRY=bundle` for its bundled CLI runtime. The probe stubs all network requests and never uses a live provider endpoint. --- ## Features - **29+ AI Models** including DeepSeek V4 Flash/Pro, GLM 5/5.1, Kimi K2.5/K2.6, Qwen3.6/3.7, MiniMax M2.7, Gemma 4, GPT-OSS, and Llama - **DeepSeek Native Thinking** — Uses the `deepseek` thinking format for Charm Hyper requests, with native `reasoning_effort` on models that publish levels - **OpenAI-compatible API** via Charm Hyper's `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint - **OAuth Device Flow** — sign in with `/login` under the `hypercharm` provider (independent of the official provider's `hyper` registration) - **Official Catalog Sync** from Charm's typed `/v1/provider` endpoint, matching `@charmland/pi-hyper-provider` — refreshed quietly in the background, at most hourly and by one pi process at a time ([details](#model-sync)) - **Reasoning Models** with provider-published on/off states and exact effort levels - **Attachment Support** for models the official catalog marks as attachment-capable ## Available Models | Model | Type | Context | Max Tokens | Input Cost | Output Cost | |-------|------|---------|------------|------------|-------------| | DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 | Text | 1.0M | 384K | $0.44 | $1.32 | | DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 | Text | 1.0M | 262K | $1.44 | $4.31 | | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | Text + Image | 1.0M | 262K | $0.33 | $1.31 | | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 | Text + Image | 1.0M | 262K | $0.33 | $1.31 | | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (Basic) | Text + Image | 1.0M | 384K | $0.20 | $0.60 | | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (Economy) | Text + Image | 1.0M | 384K | $0.20 | $0.60 | | Gemma 4 26B A4B | Text | 256K | 26K | $0.10 | $0.33 | | GLM 5.3 | Text | 1.0M | 128K | $1.52 | $4.79 | | GLM 5.3 Flash | Text + Image | 1.0M | 131K | $0.16 | $0.54 | | GLM-5.2 | Text | 1.0M | 33K | $1.52 | $4.79 | | gpt-oss-120b | Text | 131K | 13K | $0.18 | $0.68 | | Inkling | Text + Image | 1.0M | 66K | $1.09 | $4.41 | | Kimi K2 Thinking | Text | 262K | 26K | $0.60 | $2.50 | | Kimi K2.7 Code | Text + Image | 256K | 16K | $1.03 | $4.36 | | Kimi K3 | Text + Image | 1.0M | 16K | $3.27 | $16.33 | | Kimi K3.1 Pro | Text + Image | 1.0M | 262K | $2.20 | $11.00 | | MiniMax M2.7 | Text | 262K | 7K | $0.48 | $1.85 | | MiniMax M3 | Text + Image | 512K | 512K | $0.33 | $1.31 | | Muse Spark Open | Text + Image | 1.0M | 1.0M | $1.40 | $4.65 | | Prism | Text + Image | 1.0M | 131K | $2.20 | $11.00 | | Prism Core | Text + Image | 1.0M | 131K | $1.52 | $4.79 | | Prism Flash | Text + Image | 1.0M | 131K | $0.33 | $1.31 | | Qwen3.7-Flash | Text + Image | 1.0M | 64K | $0.20 | $0.80 | | Qwen3.7-Max | Text | 1.0M | 64K | $2.50 | $7.50 | | Qwen3.7-Plus | Text + Image | 1.0M | 64K | $1.20 | $4.80 | | Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B | Text | 1.0M | 128K | $2.00 | $6.00 | | Qwen3.8-27B | Text + Image | 1.0M | 128K | $0.50 | $3.00 | | Qwen3.8-Flash | Text + Image | 1.0M | 128K | $0.15 | $0.47 | | Qwen3.8-Max | Text + Image | 1.0M | 66K | $2.00 | $6.00 | *Costs are per million tokens. Prices subject to change — check [hyper.charm.land](https://hyper.charm.land) for current pricing.* ## Installation ### Option 1: Using `pi install` (Recommended) Install directly from GitHub: ```bash pi install https://github.com/monotykamary/pi-hypercharm-provider ``` Then set your API key and run pi: ```bash # Recommended: add to auth.json # See Authentication section below # Or set as environment variable export HYPERCHARM_API_KEY=your-api-key-here pi ``` Get your API key from [hyper.charm.land](https://hyper.charm.land). ### Option 2: Manual Clone 1. Clone this repository: ```bash git clone https://github.com/monotykamary/pi-hypercharm-provider.git cd pi-hypercharm-provider ``` 2. Set your HyperCharm API key: ```bash # Recommended: add to auth.json # See Authentication section below # Or set as environment variable export HYPERCHARM_API_KEY=your-api-key-here ``` 3. Run pi with the extension: ```bash pi -e /path/to/pi-hypercharm-provider ``` ## Usage After loading the extension, select a model with: ``` /model hypercharm deepseek-v4-pro ``` Or start pi directly with a HyperCharm model: ```bash pi --provider hypercharm --model deepseek-v4-pro ``` ### Reasoning Effort For reasoning models that support `reasoning_effort`, control thinking depth: ```bash pi --provider hypercharm --model deepseek-v4-pro --reasoning-effort max ``` Supported levels are model-specific and come from Charm's `/v1/provider` catalog (for example `low`/`medium`/`high` on Kimi K2.6). Models with no published levels support the Hyper thinking on state through Pi's `max` level. ### Thinking Mode DeepSeek V4 models use the `deepseek` thinking format — the same native format as the [pi-deepseek-provider](https://github.com/monotykamary/pi-deepseek-provider). This sends `thinking: {type: "enabled/disabled"}` plus `reasoning_effort` mapped via `thinkingLevelMap` (`high` → `"high"`, `max` → `"max"`). Replayed assistant messages include empty `reasoning_content` as required by DeepSeek's API. ## Footer Status A Neuralwatt-style status line sits below the editor. It appears as soon as a HyperCharm model is selected — the account side (team, balance, rate limits) renders when the session-start or model-select credits fetch lands, and the session side joins it after the first HyperCharm turn completes. Selecting another provider hides it (`hideOnOtherProvider` defaults to `true`), the balance refreshes when the agent run fully settles, and sessions that never use HyperCharm make no status-related API calls. The session-start prefetch runs only in interactive sessions (never in `pi -p` or child agents) and is shared across pi processes: one process polls and writes `~/.pi/agent/cache/hypercharm-account.json`, and sessions started within the next 2 minutes render that snapshot instead of polling again: ``` ⚡ 1.24 hc · 7 req Xu's Team ◆ 249 hc · 996/1k/h · 29d └─ session spend+requests ─┘ └─ team · balance · rate limits ──┘ ``` The left side tracks what the current session has sent/spent, read from Hyper's `usage.cost.hypercredits` extension on each response (no polling). The right side shows the team name (`/v1/teams` — works for API-key auth), the Hypercredit balance (`/v1/credits`), the per-hour and per-day request rate limits captured from response headers, and days until the OAuth device session expires when signed in with OAuth. The right side compresses progressively as the terminal narrows, and turns to a warning color at/below the `lowBalanceHc` threshold. ### Configuration Edit `~/.pi/agent/extensions/hypercharm.json` or run `/hypercharm-status`: | Setting | Values | Default | |---------|--------|---------| | `session` | `widget` \| `statusbar` \| `off` | `widget` | | `account` | `widget` \| `statusbar` \| `off` | `widget` | | `hideOnOtherProvider` | `true` \| `false` | `true` | | `lowBalanceHc` | number \| `null` | `25` | | `glyphs` | `auto` \| `unicode` \| `ascii` | `auto` | Non-interactive toggles: ``` /hypercharm-status session widget|statusbar|off /hypercharm-status account widget|statusbar|off /hypercharm-status hide true|false /hypercharm-status lowBalance 50|off /hypercharm-status glyphs auto|unicode|ascii /hypercharm-status refresh /hypercharm-status reset ``` `glyphs: "auto"` replaces the footer glyphs (bolt, gem, warning, auth arrow, separator) with ASCII equivalents on legacy terminals (mintty/Cygwin), whose cell-width tables disagree with the extension's width math. There a glyph the terminal renders wider than the extension measures overflows the widget line, which desynchronizes pi's renderer and leaves stale rows behind. The widget also right-aligns the account side flush with the terminal's last column, the way pi's built-in footer does, and clamps an explicit `unicode` choice to ASCII on legacy terminals; the statusbar is not edge-padded and always honors the exact choice. ## Authentication The HyperCharm API key can be configured in multiple ways (resolved in this order): 1. **OAuth** — Run `pi`, send `/login`, and pick **HyperCharm**. This uses Hyper's device flow (open the verification URL, enter the code) and stores a refreshable OAuth credential under the `hypercharm` provider — fully independent of the official `@charmland/pi-hyper-provider` (`hyper`) registration, so both extensions can be installed side by side. 2. **`auth.json`** (recommended for API keys) — Add to `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`: ```json { "hypercharm": { "type": "api_key", "key": "your-api-key" } } ``` The `key` field supports literal values, env var names, and shell commands (prefix with `!`). See [pi's auth file docs](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono) for details. 3. **Runtime override** — Use the `--api-key` CLI flag 4. **Environment variable** — Set `HYPERCHARM_API_KEY` Get your API key from [hyper.charm.land](https://hyper.charm.land). ## Environment Variables | Variable | Required | Description | |----------|----------|-------------| | `HYPERCHARM_API_KEY` | No | Your Charm Hyper API key (fallback if not in auth.json) | | `PI_PROVIDER_SYNC_TTL_MS` | No | Model sync freshness window in ms (default `3600000`; `0` = revalidate every session start) | ## Configuration Add to your pi configuration for automatic loading: ```json { "extensions": [ "/path/to/pi-hypercharm-provider" ] } ``` ### Catalog and Compat Settings Model metadata matches Charm's official [`@charmland/pi-hyper-provider`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/pi-hyper-provider) transform: - canonical `/v1/provider` names, prices, context windows, output caps, attachment flags, and `can_reason` - `thinkingFormat: "deepseek"`, which maps Pi thinking levels onto Hyper's `thinking` envelope - `reasoning_effort` only when the catalog publishes concrete level names - `maxTokensField: "max_tokens"` and `supportsStore: false` - `cacheRead` from `cost_per_1m_out_cached` (discounted cached-output price) and `cacheWrite` from `cost_per_1m_in_cached`, exactly as the official provider maps them - `/v1/credits` balance accepted in either hypercredits (`balance`) or USD (`balance_usd`, converted at the observed 20 hc = $1 rate) `patch.json` is reserved for verified provider regressions. It currently re-exposes Pi's `max` thinking level on the DeepSeek V4 models whose catalog `reasoning_levels` dropped it (`deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash`), matching the levels their pinned snapshots still publish. ### Patch Overrides `patch.json` is applied on top of `models.json` only for verified endpoint corrections; every other live field comes from Charm's canonical provider catalog. | Model | Override | Why | |-------|----------|-----| | `deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro` | `thinkingLevelMap.max = "max"` | The catalog now publishes only `high,xhigh`, while the pinned `-0731`/`-0813` snapshots publish `max`. | | `deepseek-v4.1-flash` | `thinkingLevelMap.max = "max"` | The catalog publishes `low,high,xhigh`; `max` mirrors the sibling DeepSeek V4 entries. | Each entry carries the model's full level map, because `patch.json` replaces `thinkingLevelMap` wholesale rather than merging it. ## Model sync Startup never waits on the network. pi starts with the cached catalog (`~/.pi/agent/cache/hypercharm-models.json`, falling back to the bundled `models.json`) and revalidates against `/v1/provider` in the background — only when: - HyperCharm credentials are configured (no credentials, no request), - the cache is older than 1 hour, missing, or was fetched with different credentials, and - no other pi process is already refreshing it (a `hypercharm-models.lock` file next to the cache). So `/new`, `/reload`, `pi -p` and fan-out child agents share one cache instead of each calling the API; a session that skips the fetch still picks up a cache another process refreshed. A failed refresh is retried after 5 minutes at the earliest. `PI_PROVIDER_SYNC_TTL_MS` changes the window (`0` revalidates on every session start). Only a hash fingerprint of the credential is stored (`hypercharm-models.sync.json`), never the credential itself. For OAuth the fingerprint follows the stored refresh token rather than the short-lived access token, so routine token refreshes do not trigger a refetch, while a completed `/login` always forces one. The footer's session-start account prefetch uses the same policy with its own cache (`hypercharm-account.json`, 2-minute window), and only in interactive sessions. ## Updating Models Run the update script to fetch the latest models from the HyperCharm API: ```bash export HYPERCHARM_API_KEY=your-api-key node scripts/update-models.js ``` This will: 1. Fetch models from `https://hyper.charm.land/v1/models` 2. Regenerate `models.json` as pure metadata from Charm's typed `/v1/provider` catalog 3. Apply overrides from `patch.json` only when building the README 4. Remove custom models now available upstream from `custom-models.json` 5. Reconcile delisted models through the 14-day `deprecated-models.json` grace layer 6. Update `models.json` and the README model table A GitHub Actions workflow runs this daily and creates a PR if models have changed. ## License MIT

It currently re-exposes Pi's `max` thinking level on the DeepSeek V4 models whose catalog `reasoning_levels` dropped it (`deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash`), matching the levels their pinned snapshots still publish. ### Patch Overrides `patch.json` is applied on top of `models.json` only for verified endpoint corrections; every other live field comes from Charm's canonical provider catalog. | Model | Override | Why | |-------|----------|-----| | `deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro` | `thinkingLevelMap.max = "max"` | The catalog now publishes only `high,xhigh`, while the pinned `-0731`/`-0813` snapshots publish `max`. | | `deepseek-v4.1-flash` | `thinkingLevelMap.max = "max"` | The catalog publishes `low,high,xhigh`; `max` mirrors the sibling DeepSeek V4 entries. | Each entry carries the model's full level map, because `patch.json` replaces `thinkingLevelMap` wholesale rather than merging it. ## Model sync Startup never waits on the network. pi starts with the cached catalog (`~/.pi/agent/cache/hypercharm-models.json`, falling back to the bundled `models.json`) and revalidates against `/v1/provider` in the background — only when: - HyperCharm credentials are configured (no credentials, no request), - the cache is older than 1 hour, missing, or was fetched with different credentials, and - no other pi process is already refreshing it (a `hypercharm-models.lock` file next to the cache). So `/new`, `/reload`, `pi -p` and fan-out child agents share one cache instead of each calling the API; a session that skips the fetch still picks up a cache another process refreshed. A failed refresh is retried after 5 minutes at the earliest. `PI_PROVIDER_SYNC_TTL_MS` changes the window (`0` revalidates on every session start). Only a hash fingerprint of the credential is stored (`hypercharm-models.sync.json`), never the credential itself. For OAuth the fingerprint follows the stored refresh token rather than the short-lived access token, so routine token refreshes do not trigger a refetch, while a completed `/login` always forces one. The footer's session-start account prefetch uses the same policy with its own cache (`hypercharm-account.json`, 2-minute window), and only in interactive sessions. ## Updating Models Run the update script to fetch the latest models from the HyperCharm API: ```bash export HYPERCHARM_API_KEY=your-api-key node scripts/update-models.js ``` This will: 1. Fetch models from `https://hyper.charm.land/v1/models` 2. Regenerate `models.json` as pure metadata from Charm's typed `/v1/provider` catalog 3. Apply overrides from `patch.json` only when building the README 4. Remove custom models now available upstream from `custom-models.json` 5. Reconcile delisted models through the 14-day `deprecated-models.json` grace layer 6. Update `models.json` and the README model table A GitHub Actions workflow runs this daily and creates a PR if models have changed. ## License MIT

Set your Wafer API key: ```bash # Recommended: add to auth.json # See Authentication section below # Or set as environment variables export WAFER_SERVERLESS_API_KEY=your-serverless-key ``` 3. A failed refresh is retried after 5 minutes at the earliest. `PI_PROVIDER_SYNC_TTL_MS` changes the window (`0` revalidates on every session start). Only a hash fingerprint of the key is stored (`wafer-serverless-models.sync.json`), never the key itself. ## License MIT

# Kimi Code CLI [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) [![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-online-blue)](https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/)
[Documentation](https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/) · [Issues](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code/issues) · [中文](README.zh-CN.md) ![Demo of using Kimi Code](./docs/media/intro.gif) ## What is Kimi Code CLI Kimi Code CLI is an AI coding agent that runs in your terminal — it can read and edit code, run shell commands, search files, fetch web pages, and choose the next step based on the feedback it receives. It works out of the box with Moonshot AI’s Kimi models and can also be configured to use other compatible providers. ## Install Install with the official script. No Node.js required. - **macOS or Linux**: ```sh curl -fsSL https://code.kimi.com/kimi-code/install.sh | bash ``` - **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell irm https://code.kimi.com/kimi-code/install.ps1 | iex ``` > On Windows, install [Git for Windows](https://gitforwindows.org/) before first launch because Kimi Code CLI uses the bundled Git Bash as its shell environment. If Git Bash is installed in a custom location, set `KIMI_SHELL_PATH` to the absolute path of `bash.exe`. Then, run it with a new shell session: ```sh kimi --version ``` For npm install, upgrade, uninstall, see [Getting Started](https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/guides/getting-started). ## Quick Start Open a project and start the interactive UI: ```sh cd your-project kimi ``` On first launch, run `/login` inside Kimi Code CLI and choose either Kimi Code OAuth or a Moonshot AI Open Platform API key. After login, try your first task: ``` Take a look at this project and explain its main directories. ``` ## Key Features - **Single-binary distribution.** Install with one command: no Node.js setup, PATH gymnastics, or global module conflicts. - **Blazing-fast startup.** The TUI is ready in milliseconds, so starting a session never feels heavy. - **Purpose-built TUI.** A carefully tuned interface, optimized end to end for long, focused agent sessions. - **Video input.** Drop a screen recording or demo clip into the chat and let the agent watch what is hard to describe in words — turn a reference clip into a LUT, a long video into a short, a screen recording into working code, and more. - **AI-native MCP configuration.** Add, edit, and authenticate Model Context Protocol servers conversationally with `/mcp-config`, without hand-editing JSON. - **Rich plugin ecosystem.** Install skills, MCP servers, and data sources from the marketplace or any GitHub repo, with each install's trust level surfaced up front. - **Subagents for focused, parallel work.** Dispatch built-in `coder`, `explore`, and `plan` subagents in isolated contexts while keeping the main conversation clean. - **Lifecycle hooks.** Run local commands at key points to gate risky tool calls, audit decisions, trigger desktop notifications, or connect to your own automation. - **Editor & IDE integration (ACP).** Drive a Kimi Code CLI session straight from Zed, JetBrains, or any [Agent Client Protocol](https://agentclientprotocol.com/) client with `kimi acp`. ## Use it in your editor (ACP) Kimi Code CLI speaks the [Agent Client Protocol](https://agentclientprotocol.com/), so ACP-compatible editors and IDEs (Zed, JetBrains, …) can drive a session over stdio. Log in once, then point your editor at the `kimi acp` subcommand — no extra login needed. For Zed, add this to `~/.config/zed/settings.json`: ```json { "agent_servers": { "Kimi Code CLI": { "type": "custom", "command": "kimi", "args": ["acp"], "env": {} } } } ``` Then open a new conversation in Zed's Agent panel. See [Using in IDEs](https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/guides/ides) for JetBrains setup and troubleshooting, and the [`kimi acp` reference](https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/reference/kimi-acp) for the full capability matrix. ## Docs - [Getting Started](https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/guides/getting-started) - [Interaction and approvals](https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/guides/interaction) - [Sessions](https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/guides/sessions) - [Using in IDEs (ACP)](https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/guides/ides) - [Configuration](https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/configuration/config-files) - [Command reference](https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/reference/kimi-command) ## Develop Requirements: Node.js ≥ 24.15.0, pnpm 10.33.0. ```sh git clone https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code.git cd kimi-code pnpm install ``` ```sh pnpm dev:cli # run the CLI in dev mode pnpm test # run tests pnpm typecheck # TypeScript check pnpm lint # oxlint pnpm build # build all packages ``` See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the full contribution guide. ## Community - [Issues](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code/issues) - For security vulnerabilities, see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Acknowledgements Our TUI is built on top of [`pi-tui`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/tree/main/packages/tui). We thank the authors of `pi-tui` for their valuable work. ## License Released under the [MIT License](LICENSE).
